The canonical-hash parity corpus test (H1/verification F-5a) pins the engine's canonical JSON form as RFC 8785 (JCS) since H5.
fixtures/canonical_hash/cases.json pins the engine's RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON form — UTF-16-sorted keys, ECMAScript number rendering — and its SHA-256 for invented inputs.
The native canonical-hash test is the blessing authority; run CANONICAL_HASH_BLESS=1 cargo test to regenerate expectations, then review the diff.

The desktop Vitest suite replays the same canonical-hash cases through the wasm exports canonical_json_string and canonical_sha256_hex, proving native and wasm lanes agree byte-for-byte on the same input text.
Canonical-hash cases carry their input as a raw JSON string so both lanes parse identical text; number rendering (1e9 to 1000000000, 200.0 to 200) is part of the pinned behavior.
The parity test imports canonical_json and sha256_hex from the open_pipe_stress_operation_applier crate.
The canonical-hash parity corpus enforces a coverage floor of at least 20 cases.
For each case the test parses input_json, computes canonical_json then sha256_hex, and asserts the result matches expected_canonical and expected_sha256.
In bless mode the test rewrites each case with the newly computed expected_canonical and expected_sha256 and writes the pretty-printed corpus back to disk.

The cross-engine operation contract corpus runner (TP-SEAM-CORPUS-001) executes every case in fixtures/model_operations/contract_corpus/ through the crate's validate_operation/apply_operation seam and asserts the recorded outcome.

The same contract corpus case files are executed by the browser-mirror engine in apps/desktop/src/services/operationContractCorpus.test.ts under the same comparison rules, holding both engines to identical semantic outcomes and one shared canonical hash.

Contract comparison uses exact equality on semantic fields: validation states, diff rows, diagnostics (code/severity/blocking/affected_refs compared order-insensitively), acceptance, audit/professional boundary, model-basis claim echoes, and identity echoes.
Engine-identity fields are excluded only via the documented allowlist: application_route, diagnostics[].id, diagnostics[].source, diagnostics[].message, diagnostics[].remediation.
Since H5 the engine canonicalization is RFC 8785 (JCS), so model_basis.backend_model_hash and applied_model_backend_hash values are now full byte-equality comparisons across every lane.
Applied model documents are compared both as parsed-JSON deep equality (numbers compared by f64 value) and by the engine's own canonical hash (canonical_json + sha256_hex).
The prior ECMA harness renderers that approximated a transport-invariant hash (Rust + TS twins) are retired because the engine rendering is now transport-invariant.
Contract corpus expected outcomes are regenerated from the Rust crate (the contract reference) via CORPUS_BLESS=1 cargo test, and blessed output requires human review before being relied on.
All contract corpus data is invented (PUBLIC_DOMAIN_OR_ORIGINAL); no protected standards content and no compliance/certification/approval claims.

The contract corpus enforces 19 required accepted operation kinds including set_field, update_load, create_node, delete_node, connect_pipe_run, create_section, create_material, create_load_case, create_combination, and delete_combination_term.

The contract corpus enforces 14 required blocking codes including OP-TARGET-ALREADY-EXISTS, OP-TARGET-NOT-FOUND, OP-UNIT-MISMATCH-CONVERSION-UNAVAILABLE, OP-STALE-BEFORE-VALUE, OP-VALUE-NOT-NUMERIC, and OP-NODE-DELETE-REFERENCED.

engine_canonical_hash returns sha256:<hex> from sha256_hex(canonical_json(value)); since H5 the JCS canonicalization is transport-invariant so one formula serves both blessed-value comparison and engine self-consistency.
json_semantically_equal performs parsed-JSON deep equality with numbers compared by f64 value so an integer literal and the same float literal compare equal.
semantic_outcome projects the engine outcome onto the cross-engine semantic comparison surface, mirrored exactly by semanticOutcome in the Vitest runner.
Projected diagnostics are reduced to code/severity/blocking/affected_refs and sorted by a stable diagnostic_sort_key combining code, affected_refs, and severity.
run_case asserts the input base_model is never mutated by validate_operation or apply_operation by comparing it to a pre-call snapshot.

For applied cases the test asserts the applied model deep-equals the expected document, the engine canonical hash matches the recorded hash, and applied_model_backend_hash byte-equals the blessed hash in every lane (H5 full byte-equality).
For blocked applies the test asserts no applied_model, no recorded applied-model hash, and no applied_model_backend_hash.

The corpus coverage test asserts every required accepted kind and every required blocking code is exercised, plus accepted and blocked cases for dynamic paths primitive_loads.N.magnitude.value and terms.N.factor.
The validation_preview package provides operation validation and deterministic diff preview helpers.
validation_preview exports PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY, VALIDATION_PREVIEW_VERSION, canonical_json, and validate_and_preview_operations from its engine module.
The validation preview engine (DEL-16-02) validates proposed operation records and produces deterministic preview deltas against an accepted model-state snapshot.
The validation preview engine never mutates the accepted input state and never treats a preview as an accepted technical result.
VALIDATION_PREVIEW_VERSION is 0.1.0.
Supported operation kinds are add, move, modify, delete, reconnect, constraint, load, support, and design_knowledge.
Supported change kinds are add_object, remove_object, set_field, move_geometry, reconnect, update_constraint, update_load, update_support, and attach_design_knowledge.

The validation preview engine defines a canonical dimension vocabulary including dimensionless, length, force, moment, pressure, stress, second_moment_area, section_modulus, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, and TBD.
PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY records human_review_required=True and that the software makes no compliance, certification, sealing, approval, or authentication claim.

ENGINE_PROVENANCE records source name, location, project-governed license, contributor certification implementation-only-no-professional-claim, public_permissive redistribution, pending review, and public_metadata privacy.
validate_and_preview_operations validates a structured operation envelope against an accepted model state and returns a deterministic preview, accepting optional constraint_diagnostics.
The engine deep-copies the accepted model state as its working source_state so the original input is never mutated.
The engine aggregates diagnostics from envelope validation, schema validation, model-basis checks, and constraint diagnostics.
An operation with any blocking diagnostic produces a blocked preview row and its changes are not previewed.
The preview result is tagged deliverable DEL-16-02, package PKG-16, scope SOW-069, and objective OBJ-015.
The result validation block reports schema_validation, constraint_validation, unit_validation, diff_preview_status, and application_status, with application_status set to not_applied.
diff_preview rows are sorted by canonical_json and diagnostics are stably sorted; the result also reports accepted_model_state_unchanged.
canonical_json serializes preview output as JSON with sort_keys=True, compact separators, and ensure_ascii=True for stable key ordering.
Operation validation requires the envelope deliverable_id to be DEL-16-01, otherwise it emits OP-UPSTREAM-SCHEMA-BINDING; validation consumes DEL-16-01 structured operation records.
The envelope must contain schema_version, deliverable_id, package_id, scope_item, objectives, and operation_set; each missing field emits OP-ENVELOPE-FIELD-MISSING.
Schema diagnostics validate the envelope against schemas/model_operation.schema.json using a JSON Schema 2020-12 validator; a missing validator emits OP-SCHEMA-VALIDATOR-MISSING.

Model-basis diagnostics require the operation set to bind to a physical_source_of_truth model role and a current model-state hash, emitting OP-MODEL-BASIS-MISSING or OP-MODEL-ROLE-BLOCKED when absent or wrong.
When the operation model-basis accepted_model_state_hash does not match the current accepted model state hash, the engine emits OP-MODEL-BASIS-HASH-MISMATCH.
Each operation must include preconditions with a required_current_hashes entry scoped to model_state_record matching the current state hash, else OP-CURRENT-HASH-MISSING or OP-CURRENT-HASH-MISMATCH.
An operation_kind outside SUPPORTED_OPERATION_KINDS emits OP-KIND-UNSUPPORTED.
An operation that requests direct accepted-model mutation emits OP-DIRECT-MUTATION-BLOCKED; operations stay structured proposals for validation, preview, and later user review.
A change_kind outside SUPPORTED_CHANGE_KINDS emits OP-CHANGE-KIND-UNSUPPORTED.
A change missing a structured value_payload mapping emits OP-PAYLOAD-MISSING.
Quantity-kind payloads require complete value, unit, and dimension metadata, emitting OP-UNIT-METADATA-MISSING when incomplete.
Quantity payloads whose dimension is outside the accepted PKG-02 vocabulary emit OP-UNIT-DIMENSION-UNKNOWN.
For remove_object, set_field, move_geometry, and reconnect changes, a target id absent from the entity index emits OP-TARGET-REF-UNRESOLVED.

_preview_change computes a deterministic before/after delta: add_object builds an object from payload, remove_object sets after to None, otherwise it patches the existing object, and unresolved targets are blocked_by_validation.
_blocked_preview emits a preview row with change_kind blocked_by_validation and the sorted blocking diagnostic codes.
_entity_index builds an id-keyed map of accepted-state entities, reading from entities or model_state.entities.
_patched_object applies structured_values, scalar_values, and quantity_values from the payload as preview overlays on a deep copy of the entity.
_direct_mutation_requested flags operations whose validation application_status is outside the allowed set or whose operation_status is agent_accepted_engineering_state or auto_approved.
_quantity_has_units treats a mapping as having units only when it contains value, unit, and dimension keys.

The solver-boundary adapter accepts canonical analytical_solver_model mappings and emits plain deterministic records for lower solver-boundary orchestration; it is not a public API, CLI, preview runtime, or load engine.
The adapter contract id is DEL-13-04-internal-analytical-solver-boundary-adapter-0.1, with axes (X,Y,Z), DOF axes (UX,UY,UZ,RX,RY,RZ), and a vector tolerance of 1.0e-12.

LOAD_RECORD_CONTRACTS defines four canonical load record types: nodal_force, nodal_moment, element_point_force, and element_uniform_distributed_force, each with required keys, target type, quantity dimension, and direction axes.

Material property dimensions require elastic_modulus and shear_modulus as stress; section property dimensions require area, second_moment_y, second_moment_z, and torsion_constant; mass_per_length is optional.

SolverBoundaryAdapterResult is a frozen dataclass DTO carrying nodes, straight_pipe_connectivity, property_bindings, support_targets, load_case_records, load_applications, adapter_dto_records, and diagnostics.
SolverBoundaryAdapterResult.has_blocking_findings is True when any diagnostic or load-case diagnostic has severity blocking.
adapt_analytical_solver_model adapts a strict analytical solver model into deterministic DTO records.
A non-mapping analytical model input emits blocking ASBA-SOURCE-MODEL-MISSING and returns an empty result.
An analytical model whose model_role is not analytical_solver_model emits blocking ASBA-SOURCE-ROLE-UNEXPECTED.

_adapt_nodes requires id, coordinates, and degrees_of_freedom, emits ASBA-NODE-DOF-UNRESOLVED when any DOF axis is None/empty/TBD, and adapts each node into indexed coordinate values, units, and quantities.

_adapt_straight_pipes requires straight_pipe elements with resolvable start/end node, material, section, and a canonical cartesian local_coordinate_system; non-straight-pipe types emit ASBA-ELEMENT-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED.
Straight-pipe connectivity requires an explicit cartesian local coordinate system; absence emits ASBA-ELEMENT-LOCAL-COORDINATE-SYSTEM-UNSUPPORTED.
The local_coordinate_system must contain exactly type, axes, y_reference, and provenance; extra keys emit ASBA-ELEMENT-LOCAL-COORDINATE-SYSTEM-NONCANONICAL.
Local axes other than canonical X/Y/Z emit ASBA-ELEMENT-LOCAL-AXES-UNSUPPORTED.
An adapted straight pipe records derived_axis_x from start/end coordinates, the y_reference vector, and solver_orientation_status governed_y_reference_ready.
_adapt_property_bindings binds each straight pipe to its required material and section quantity properties plus optional section properties, producing a BIND-STRAIGHT-PIPE binding record.

_adapt_supports requires id, support_type, target_ref, directions, and properties; directions must be explicit DOF axes (ASBA-SUPPORT-DIRECTIONS-UNSUPPORTED) and the target must resolve to an adapted node or element (ASBA-SUPPORT-TARGET-UNRESOLVED).

_adapt_load_cases validates each load case and its loads, emitting load applications only for fully canonical resolvable loads and marking the load case solver_ready only when all loads emit with no diagnostics.
A load record_type not in the canonical union emits ASBA-LOAD-RECORD-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED, and noncanonical extra keys emit ASBA-LOAD-NONCANONICAL-SEMANTICS-UNSUPPORTED.
Each load's quantity must match the contract quantity dimension and its direction must be in the contract direction axes (ASBA-LOAD-DIRECTION-UNSUPPORTED).
element_point_force loads require a dimensionless station_fraction quantity; element_uniform_distributed_force loads require a validated span.
_orientation_diagnostics validates that a finite nonzero local X axis exists and that y_reference is three finite numeric components, nonzero, and not parallel to the derived X axis.
_derived_axis_x returns the normalized direction vector between two 3D coordinate lists, or None when the separation length is within tolerance.

_span requires start_fraction and end_fraction dimensionless quantities, both in [0,1] with start_fraction < end_fraction, emitting span range and order diagnostics since JSON Schema cannot compare sibling values.
_norm computes the Euclidean norm and _cross computes the 3D vector cross product.
_adapter_dto_identity_records builds a sorted DTO identity record per load application with a JCS sha256 payload_hash and a two-step source_chain from analytical model to adapter DTO to solver input.
_stable_payload_hash computes a sha256 hex digest over the JSON-encoded value with sorted keys, compact separators, and allow_nan=False.

_quantity validates a canonical Quantity requiring value, unit, dimension, and provenance, a finite numeric value, explicit non-TBD unit/dimension, and a matching expected dimension, with a distinct diagnostic per failure.
The adapter does not convert or infer units and does not reinterpret dimensions; a quantity dimension mismatch emits a DIMENSION-UNSUPPORTED diagnostic.
_ref builds an object reference mapping of object_type and id with spaces replaced by hyphens.
The adapter _diagnostic record carries code, class (SOLVE_BLOCKING or ASSUMPTION_WARNING), severity, source, affected_object, message, and remediation.
The physical-to-analytical transform contract derives a solver-oriented centerline/frame model from a supplied physical source model and is provider-neutral.
Incomplete or non-representable inputs become deterministic diagnostics instead of inferred engineering defaults.
Centerline element types are straight_pipe, frame, and rigid; supported analytical metadata component types are rigid, valve, flange, reducer, and specialty.
Supported support types are anchor, guide, line_stop, restraint, spring, gap, and friction.
TransformSettings carries stable analytical_model_id, analytical_model_name, and contract_version DEL-13-04-0.1 into deterministic output identity.
TransformResult carries the analytical_model, diagnostics, and traceability_links, with has_blocking_findings True when any diagnostic severity is blocking.
transform_physical_to_analytical derives a deterministic analytical model from a physical source model without mutating the source; non-representable records are omitted with traceable diagnostics.
A non-mapping physical model input emits blocking PTA-SOURCE-MODEL-MISSING and returns an empty analytical model.
A physical model whose model_role is not physical_source_of_truth emits the warning PTA-SOURCE-ROLE-UNEXPECTED.
A missing or TBD coordinate_system emits blocking PTA-COORDINATE-SYSTEM-MISSING; the transform does not infer a coordinate system.

The derived analytical model has model_role analytical_solver_model and carries nodes, elements, components, materials, sections, supports, load_cases, combinations, stable diagnostics, and traceability links.
_copy_nodes requires id, coordinates, and degrees_of_freedom with resolved unit and DOF gaps; an absent or empty node list emits blocking PTA-NODES-MISSING.
_copy_records_with_units copies materials and sections only when their quantity-bearing fields have resolved unit metadata, emitting unit gap diagnostics otherwise.
_classify_components requires id, component_type, geometry, mechanics_modifiers, and provenance; unsupported component types emit the warning PTA-COMPONENT-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED and are excluded.

_copy_elements validates element fields and references, blocking on unresolved node/material/section refs and on component_ref that does not resolve to a supported analytical metadata component (PTA-ELEMENT-COMPONENT-UNSUPPORTED).
An element_type outside the centerline/frame types emits the warning PTA-ELEMENT-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED unless it is a component_link to a known component.
_copy_supports validates support fields and target references and emits PTA-SUPPORT-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED for support types outside the supported set.
_copy_load_cases validates load case fields and each load's target reference and quantity units, blocking on unresolved targets or unit gaps.

_quantity_gaps recursively inspects unit-bearing values, emitting a unit diagnostic for missing/TBD unit or dimension and PTA-UNIT-DIMENSION-UNKNOWN for dimensions outside the accepted PKG-02 vocabulary.
_dof_gaps requires a degrees_of_freedom mapping with explicit non-TBD states for all six DOF axes, emitting PTA-NODE-DOF-MISSING or PTA-NODE-DOF-UNRESOLVED; no restraint defaults are inferred.
_reference_gap emits a blocking SOLVE_BLOCKING diagnostic when a referenced record id is missing or not present among known ids.
_trace_link builds a physical_to_analytical traceability link from source to target (or to a synthesized Diagnostic target) with provenance.
_stable_traceability deterministically orders links and attaches the matching diagnostic to links whose target object_type is Diagnostic.
The contract _ref coerces object_type to TBD unless it is one of the known types Project, Model, Node, Element, Component, Material, Section, Support, LoadCase, Combination, or Diagnostic.
The open_pipe_stress_product_physics crate (version 0.1.0, edition 2021, publish=false) is the product-preview physics adapter for OpenPipeStress.
product_physics depends on the frame_kernel, load_case_algebra, linear_supports, primitive_loads, straight_pipe, stress_recovery, and units crates plus serde and serde_json.
The product_physics preview_result example loads the invented_preview_model.json fixture into a PreviewModel.
The preview example runs run_linear_static_preview with an empty materials list and prints the pretty-printed JSON result.
Crate core/product_physics is a product-preview physics adapter mapping invented public preview-model data into the code-neutral mechanics crates.
The physics adapter emits mechanics quantities and diagnostics only; it does not encode standards criteria, allowables, SIF tables, private data, or professional acceptance.
PreviewModel is the deserialized preview input: schema_version, document_kind, project, analysis_status, nodes, pipe_segments, supports, materials, load_cases, and combinations.
StatusEnvelope carries three status strings: mechanics, rule_check, and professional_acceptance.
PreviewNode has an id, a position (Vec3), and optional provenance.
Vec3 is a 3D coordinate with f64 x, y, z fields.
PreviewPipe references from-node and to-node ids, a section, a material id, an optional y_reference orientation vector, and optional provenance.
PipeSectionInput specifies outside_diameter and wall_thickness as unit-bearing Quantity values.
Quantity is a unit-bearing scalar with an f64 value and a unit string.
PreviewSupport has an id, a node reference, a list of restraint DOF strings, an optional family, optional stiffness input, and optional provenance.
PreviewLoadCase has an id, a list of primitive_loads, and optional provenance.
PreviewCombination has an id, optional label, a basis string, terms, and optional minuend_id, subtrahend_id, operand_ids, mode, and provenance.
The combination basis is a closed set: mechanics (linear terms), result_state_subtraction (minuend minus subtrahend), and range_envelope (mode over operand_ids); vocabulary mirrors AlgebraExpression.
PreviewCombinationTerm pairs a load_case id with an f64 factor.
PreviewPrimitiveLoad has id, category, target, direction, magnitude (Quantity), dimension, and optional provenance.
LoadTargetInput is a tagged enum selecting either a Node target or an Element (pipe) target.
MaterialInput carries id, elastic_modulus, shear_modulus, optional thermal_expansion_coefficient, and optional provenance.
LinearStaticPreviewRequest wraps a PreviewModel plus an optional materials list.
MechanicsEnvelope is the emitted result: schema_version, document_kind, run_id, model_ref, status, summary, results, diagnostics, professional_boundary, and accepted_model_state_mutated.
Summary reports node_count, segment_count, support_count, load_case_count, and optional max_displacement and max_open_formula_stress.
LocatedQuantity is a value with unit, a location_ref, and a result_ref.
ResultItem is a single result row: id, kind, value, unit, entity_ref, optional basis_ref, source_result_refs, and optional metadata.
ResultBasisRef pairs a ref_type with a ref_id.
ResultMetadata records component, coordinate_system, location, basis, and sign_convention for a result row.
Diagnostic is a finding row: id, code, severity, message, optional source, and affected_refs.
ProfessionalBoundary flags human_review_required and four software-claim booleans for compliance, certification, sealing, and approval.
DerivedSection holds computed pipe section properties: area, internal_area, second_moment, torsion_constant, section_modulus, torsion_radius, membrane_radius, and wall_thickness.
run_linear_static_preview is the public entry point that validates inputs, normalizes units, builds the model, applies boundary conditions, solves each load case, and assembles the MechanicsEnvelope.
When request.materials is empty the adapter falls back to the model's own materials list.
The adapter requires document_kind to equal openpipestress.product_preview.model, else emits a blocking PREVIEW_DOCUMENT_KIND_INVALID diagnostic.
An empty schema_version yields a blocking PREVIEW_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISSING diagnostic; the preview model requires an explicit schema version.
If any blocking diagnostic is present the adapter returns a blocked envelope rather than solving.

Linear-static preview requires explicit support restraints or springs; with no restraints and no springs a blocking SUPPORT_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic is emitted and no automatic boundary conditions are applied.
Fewer than six rigid restraints (DOF_PER_NODE) yields a blocking SOLVER_SYSTEM_BLOCKED under-restrained diagnostic naming restrained, missing, and per-support DOF contributions.
Boundary-preparation findings are surfaced as blocking SUPPORT_INPUT_INVALID diagnostics keyed by support id.
Global stiffness is assembled from the frame elements; assembly failure returns a solver-blocked envelope.
Spring supports add their stiffness value to the diagonal of the global stiffness matrix at the spring's global DOF index.
Each load case is solved independently; a frame-kernel error during a load-case solve returns a solver-blocked envelope.
Summary max_displacement and max_stress are taken from the first (default) load-case solve.
Result rows are indexed by base id and load-case id; non-default load cases get qualified result ids and a load_case basis_ref.
A computed max displacement exceeding 5.0 (invented review threshold) emits a HIGH_DISPLACEMENT_REVIEW warning diagnostic.
The adapter always appends a RULE_CHECK_INPUTS_MISSING warning: rule-check inputs and protected criteria are absent, so no compliance result is produced.

A solved MechanicsEnvelope sets document_kind openpipestress.product_preview.mechanics_result, schema_version 0.1.0, mechanics status MECHANICS_SOLVED, rule_check RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, and professional_acceptance NOT_PROVIDED.
A successful preview run leaves accepted_model_state_mutated false; the adapter does not mutate accepted model state.
solve_load_case builds primitive loads, prepares the load application, assembles the force vector, reduces and solves the linear system, and recovers displacements, reactions, forces, and stresses.
Load-application findings are surfaced as blocking LOAD_INPUT_INVALID diagnostics keyed by load id and load-case id.
Thermal element loads and pressure-thrust loads are derived and added to the force vector alongside uniform element loads.
The reduced system is solved with reduce_system and solve_dense; reduced displacements are scattered back into the full free-DOF displacement vector.
Per-node displacement magnitude is computed and reported in millimetres, tracking the maximum displacement across nodes.
Support reactions are computed as internal minus applied force (K*u - f) and reported as a reaction resultant magnitude in newtons over the support's restrained DOFs.
Per-pipe element local forces are recovered from the global solution; recovery failure emits a warning ELEMENT_FORCE_RECOVERY_FAILED diagnostic and skips the element.
Recovered local forces are corrected for thermal and pressure-thrust axial effects before force and stress results are appended.
Force and stress results are produced at endpoints (end_i, end_j) and at interpolated stations along the element.
When pressure thrust is active the pressure longitudinal stress component is excluded from the open-formula stress (include_pressure_longitudinal is false).
Stress-recovery findings emit warning STRESS_RECOVERY_LIMITED diagnostics; endpoint and station stress results are only appended when their findings are empty.
The per-element open_formula_stress_summary is the maximum open-formula stress (in MPa) across endpoints and stations, tracked as the load case max stress.
build_model constructs frame nodes, straight-pipe elements, derived sections, and linear supports from the preview model and materials.
Invalid node coordinates emit a blocking NODE_INPUT_INVALID diagnostic.
A pipe whose from-node or to-node is absent from the model emits a blocking PIPE_ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN diagnostic.
A pipe material with no matching MaterialInput emits a blocking MATERIAL_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic; pipe material requires explicit elastic and shear modulus inputs and no defaults are applied.
A pipe without an explicit y_reference vector emits a blocking PIPE_ORIENTATION_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic; no default orientation is applied.
Pipe section properties are built from material moduli and derived geometric properties; invalid section properties emit a blocking PIPE_SECTION_INPUT_INVALID diagnostic.
A support with family spring is built as a spring support using its first DOF and parsed stiffness; a support with six restrained DOFs is an anchor; otherwise it is a guide support.
normalize_model_units converts material moduli, thermal expansion coefficient, pipe diameter and wall thickness, support stiffness, and load magnitudes to their canonical solver units.

normalize_quantity converts a unit-bearing quantity to the dimension's canonical unit, emitting a UNIT_CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic on unknown symbol, missing canonical unit, or conversion failure.
normalize_quantity skips conversion for non-finite quantity values.
UNIT_CONVERSION_UNAVAILABLE is blocking: preview mechanics could not normalize unit-bearing input to the DEC-018 SI-canonical solver boundary.
build_load_case_primitive_loads parses each load's category, direction, and dimension and maps it to a nodal or element PrimitiveLoad.
An authored load category mapped to a preview category emits a warning LOAD_CATEGORY_PREVIEW_MAPPED diagnostic; the preview classification is not a user-selected engineering classification.
A non-finite load magnitude emits a blocking LOAD_MAGNITUDE_INVALID diagnostic; load magnitude must be finite.
A load targeting an unknown node emits a blocking LOAD_NODE_UNKNOWN diagnostic.
A load targeting an unknown pipe emits a blocking LOAD_PIPE_UNKNOWN diagnostic.
An unsupported load category, direction, or dimension emits a blocking LOAD_INPUT_INVALID diagnostic.
derive_pipe_section validates outside diameter and wall thickness, requiring explicit positive values with wall thickness less than radius, else emits a blocking PIPE_DIMENSION_INVALID diagnostic.
Inside diameter is computed as outside diameter minus twice the wall thickness (id = od - 2*t).
Pipe cross-sectional area is PI*(od^2 - id^2)/4.
Pipe internal (bore) area is PI*id^2/4.
Pipe second moment of area is PI*(od^4 - id^4)/64.
Pipe torsion constant is twice the second moment of area (2*I).
Pipe section modulus is the second moment of area divided by the outer radius (I/(od/2)).
Torsion radius is the outer radius od/2; membrane radius is (od - t)/2.
add_uniform_element_loads distributes element uniform loads equally to the two end nodes (half the magnitude times length to each end), skipping pressure and temperature-change dimensions.
build_thermal_element_loads computes an equivalent axial load E*A*alpha*deltaT for thermal temperature-change loads on elements with a defined thermal expansion coefficient.
build_pressure_thrust_loads computes a pressure-thrust axial load as pressure magnitude times the internal (bore) area for pressure-dimension element loads.
add_pressure_thrust_loads applies the pressure-thrust axial load along the element local x axis, subtracting at node i and adding at node j.
add_thermal_equivalent_loads applies the thermal equivalent axial load along the element local x axis, subtracting at node i and adding at node j.
corrected_local_forces_for_axial_effects adds the summed thermal and pressure-thrust axial load into the recovered local axial force at both element ends.
Station resultants are evaluated at three interior locations: quarter_1 (0.25), midspan (0.5), and quarter_3 (0.75) along the element.
Station resultants are linearly interpolated between end_i and end_j resultants by the station fraction.
Per-node displacement components (ux, uy, uz in mm; rx, ry, rz in rad) are reported in the global coordinate system with explicit sign conventions.
Element force and moment results (axial, shear-y, shear-z in N; torsion, bending-y, bending-z in N*m) are reported at each endpoint in the element-local coordinate system.
recover_endpoint_stress recovers stress components from endpoint force resultants, section properties, and optional pressure basis via recover_stresses.
recover_station_stress recovers stress components from interpolated station resultants, section properties, and optional pressure basis.

The open-formula stress summary (MPa) is the larger absolute extreme-fibre normal stress: max(|base_normal + bending_total|, |base_normal - bending_total|), where base_normal = axial + pressure-longitudinal and bending_total = |bending_y| + |bending_z|.
Endpoint stress results report axial-normal, bending-normal-y, bending-normal-z, and torsional-shear components, plus pressure hoop and longitudinal stresses when pressure is present.
CombinationExpression is a per-basis expression over solved load-case result rows whose variants mirror AlgebraExpression: Mechanics, ResultStateSubtraction, and RangeEnvelope.

CombinationExpression::resolve maps a PreviewCombination basis string to an expression: mechanics requires non-empty terms, subtraction requires minuend and subtrahend ids, range_envelope requires non-empty operand ids and a parsed mode.
Range-envelope operand ids are sorted to a deterministic order before evaluation.
Operand ids define deterministic source-lookup order: authored term order for mechanics, minuend then subtrahend for subtraction, and sorted operand ids for range envelope.
The reference operand supplies result identity (kind, unit, entity, metadata) for the combined row.
append_combination_results applies each combination to each base result id, combining matching source rows across load cases and appending qualified combination result rows.
A missing reference source row emits a warning LOAD_COMBINATION_SOURCE_RESULT_MISSING diagnostic.
Open-formula stress summary rows are not linearly combined (COMBINATION_STRESS_SUMMARY_SKIPPED warning); combine inspectable stress component rows instead.
Result rows whose unit is unsupported for scalar load-combination algebra emit a warning LOAD_COMBINATION_RESULT_DIMENSION_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic.
Combination source rows must match kind, unit, entity, and result metadata; a mismatch emits a warning LOAD_COMBINATION_SOURCE_RESULT_MISMATCH diagnostic and skips the combination.
A blocked algebra result surfaces its findings as combination warning diagnostics rather than producing a combined row.
A combined result row clones the reference row, sets a qualified combination id, the algebra value, a combination basis_ref, source_result_refs, and basis/sign-convention metadata.
algebra_dimension maps result units to load dimensions: mm->Displacement, rad->Rotation, N->Force, N*m->Moment, MPa->Pressure.
algebra_finding_diagnostic_code maps each algebra FindingCode to its named combination diagnostic code.
blocked_envelope returns a MechanicsEnvelope with mechanics status MODEL_INCOMPLETE, no results, and the accumulated diagnostics.
solver_blocked appends a blocking SOLVER_SYSTEM_BLOCKED diagnostic for a frame-kernel error and returns a blocked envelope.
pressure_for_pipe sums the magnitudes of pressure-dimension element loads targeting a pipe, returning None when no pressure load is found.
displacement_magnitude is the Euclidean norm of the node's UX, UY, UZ translational displacements.
parse_dof maps DOF strings (UX/UY/UZ/RX/RY/RZ, case-insensitive) to FrameDof, erroring on unsupported tokens.
parse_direction maps global_x/global_y/global_z to LoadDirection global axes, otherwise parses a DOF-based direction.
parse_category maps preview load category strings to PrimitiveLoadCategory, treating distributed_force as Weight and concentrated_force/concentrated_moment as Occasional.
authored_category_preview_mapping reports the preview category an authored category maps to: concentrated_force/concentrated_moment to occasional, distributed_force to weight.
parse_load_dimension maps preview dimension strings (force, moment, force_per_length, pressure, temperature_change/temperature_interval, acceleration, displacement, rotation) to LoadDimension.
expected_load_dimension maps load dimension strings to the units-crate Dimension for normalization.
is_temperature_change_dimension is true for temperature_change and temperature_interval.
professional_boundary always sets human_review_required true and all software compliance, certification, sealing, and approval claim flags false.
stable_suffix replaces colons with hyphens in an id to form a stable diagnostic/result suffix.
round6 rounds a value to six decimal places and normalizes negative zero to positive zero.
core/product_physics/src/lib.rs includes a cfg(test) module of unit tests over the invented preview fixture.
Test contract: a valid invented model solves deterministically to MECHANICS_SOLVED with non-empty results and a positive max displacement.
Test contract: authored primitive categories (concentrated_force, concentrated_moment, distributed_force) map to preview mechanics categories and surface a LOAD_CATEGORY_PREVIEW_MAPPED warning.
validate_model_inputs runs the full input validation suite: required collections, ids, provenance, units, thermal inputs, and combinations.
Linear-static preview requires at least two explicit nodes, else a blocking NODE_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic.
Linear-static preview requires at least one explicit pipe segment, else a blocking PIPE_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic.
Linear-static preview requires at least one explicit primitive load, else a blocking LOAD_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic; no hidden loads are applied.
validate_ids checks node, pipe, support, material, load-case, primitive-load, and combination ids for duplicates and emptiness.
validate_provenance requires every node, pipe, support, material, load case, primitive load, and combination to carry public-preview provenance.

validate_units checks that material moduli, thermal expansion coefficient, pipe diameter and wall thickness, support stiffness, and load magnitudes carry units compatible with their expected dimension.
detect_empty_ids emits a blocking EMPTY_ID diagnostic for any blank id; every entity ID must be explicit and non-empty.
detect_duplicate_ids emits a blocking DUPLICATE_ID diagnostic for repeated ids; entity IDs must be unique within the preview mechanics model.
expect_public_preview_provenance requires provenance text containing 'invented' or 'cleared'; missing or non-conforming provenance emits a blocking PROVENANCE_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic.
expect_unit emits a blocking UNIT_INPUT_INVALID diagnostic when a quantity's unit is incompatible with its expected dimension, naming the canonical unit.
validate_thermal_inputs requires that thermal temperature-change loads have an explicit, finite material thermal_expansion_coefficient; no hidden material defaults are applied.
Thermal loads with a missing thermal_expansion_coefficient emit a blocking THERMAL_EXPANSION_INPUT_MISSING diagnostic.
A non-finite thermal_expansion_coefficient emits a blocking THERMAL_EXPANSION_INPUT_INVALID diagnostic.

validate_combinations dispatches per basis to mechanics, subtraction, or range-envelope validation, emitting a blocking LOAD_COMBINATION_BASIS_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic for any basis outside the closed set.
Notes: Code/rule and owner-basis combinations remain private/deferred

UnitStatement: expect_known_combination_load_case emits a blocking LOAD_COMBINATION_LOAD_CASE_UNKNOWN diagnostic when a combination references a load case absent from the model.

Mechanics-basis combinations carry explicit terms only and require at least one term; subtraction/range fields present, empty terms, or non-finite factors emit blocking shape/terms/factor diagnostics.
result_state_subtraction combinations require exactly a non-empty minuend_id and subtrahend_id; missing, extra-field, or self-subtraction shapes emit blocking diagnostics.
range_envelope combinations require operand_ids and a mode from the closed set min/max/min_abs/max_abs; empty or duplicate operands and unknown modes emit blocking diagnostics.
core/product_preview is the local product-preview service for the macOS technical preview.

product_preview re-exports build_analysis_run_preview, build_agent_proposal_preview, build_model_tree, build_report_packet_preview, load_design_knowledge, load_preview_model, run_preview_mechanics, and validate_preview_model from its service module.

core/product_preview/service.py provides schema-adjacent service functions for the invented desktop product preview; it stays local and deterministic and runs no external solvers or hidden model mutations.
PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY constant asserts human_review_required=True and that the software makes no compliance, certification, sealing, or approval claims.

PROHIBITED_TEXT lists guardrail phrases (e.g. 'code compliant','certified','sealed','professional approval','approved for construction','release ready','production ready') that must not appear in preview output.
load_preview_model() loads the invented preview model fixture invented_preview_model.json.
run_preview_mechanics() returns a deterministic mechanics/status envelope from an invented result fixture; it does not run external solver/prover execution or rule-pack checking.
run_preview_mechanics attaches PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY and sets accepted_model_state_mutated=False on its result.
build_analysis_run_preview() builds an immutable analysis-run record from the preview mechanics result, with preview model-state, solver-settings, and SI unit-system refs.
build_report_packet_preview() materializes read-only report-packet context; it is not a rendered calculation report, export adapter payload, compliance result, or professional acceptance record.

The preview report packet records professional_boundary, a privacy_boundary (invented_public_example, no private/protected payload, telemetry disallowed), and report_packet_status flags marking it read-only context only.
build_agent_proposal_preview() returns a deterministic non-mutating proposal preview with application_status='not_applied' and accepted_model_state_mutated=False.
build_model_tree() builds tree/inspector input records for the desktop UI from nodes, pipe_segments, supports, and components.
validate_preview_model() validates the bounded product-preview shape and guardrail text, returning structured diagnostics.

Preview validation emits blocking diagnostics PREVIEW_DOCUMENT_KIND_INVALID, PREVIEW_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISSING, and PREVIEW_GEOMETRY_INCOMPLETE when document_kind, schema_version, or geometry (nodes/pipe_segments) are missing.
Combination validation requires basis=='mechanics' and non-empty terms, and emits blocking diagnostics for unsupported basis, empty terms, unknown referenced load_case, and non-finite factor.
Pipe-segment validation flags PREVIEW_PIPE_ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN when from/to nodes are unknown and PREVIEW_UNIT_METADATA_MISSING when outside_diameter or wall_thickness lack value/unit metadata.
Support validation emits PREVIEW_SUPPORT_NODE_UNKNOWN when a support's node is not a known node id.
Preview validation serializes the record to canonical JSON and emits PREVIEW_PROHIBITED_CLAIM_TEXT for any PROHIBITED_TEXT phrase found.
canonical_json() returns deterministic JSON via json.dumps with sort_keys=True, compact separators, and ensure_ascii=True.
hash_ref() returns a sha256 hash record over canonical JSON of a payload with algorithm 'sha256' and canonicalization 'JCS'.
_validate_identity_and_provenance() requires a non-empty id and a provenance containing 'invented' or 'cleared', else emits PREVIEW_ID_MISSING or PREVIEW_PROVENANCE_MISSING.
core/project_persistence/__init__.py exposes project persistence service helpers for TP-PER-01.

project_persistence package re-exports its public API including build/validate/round_trip persistence envelope, create/open/save/migrate/version_check project store, hash manifest, and retrieval sidecar helpers.

core/project_persistence/service.py builds deterministic project persistence envelopes and implements the SCA-003 MVP local SQLite store/index profile, where canonical JSON/JCS payload bytes remain the domain truth.
Persistence service constants define DOCUMENT_KIND 'openpipestress.project_persistence', schema refs, SQLITE_STORE_PROFILE 'sqlite_local_project_store', and SQLITE_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION '1'.
Persistence PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY requires human_review_required=True and denies compliance, certification, sealing, approval, and authentication claims.
PRIVATE_DATA_MARKER classifies persisted payloads as public_permissive with default_transmission_allowed=False and quarantine_required=False.
ENGINE_PROVENANCE records source name/location, project-governed license, contributor certification 'implementation-only-no-professional-claim', and public_permissive redistribution.

physical_container_profile() returns the accepted SCA-003 container: SQLite local store/index projection where SQL is not a public contract, direct SQL access and hosted DB are disallowed, no network is required, and sidecars are rebuildable.
retrieval_sidecar_manifest() returns a default non-authoritative, rebuildable, hash-neutral local sqlite_fts5_bm25 retrieval sidecar that can be deleted and rebuilt from canonical payloads.
build_project_persistence_envelope() builds a deterministic persistence envelope around a canonical model, assembling project, migration, validation_profile, service_operations, and a content hash.

The persistence envelope's round_trip_manifest declares canonical_json_jcs serialization, lists semantically-equal fields, empty volatile_fields, and normalization rules (schema_approved_only, no_silent_engineering_defaults, documented_volatile_field_exclusion).
The validation_profile enables schema, unit-metadata, provenance, rule-pack-reference, protected-content, private-data, and professional-boundary checks with telemetry_default 'off'.
validate_project_persistence_envelope() returns structured diagnostics for TP-PER-01 persistence invariants.
Persistence validation emits PERSISTENCE_FIELD_MISSING for missing schema_version, document_kind, project, hash, or migration, and PERSISTENCE_DOCUMENT_KIND_INVALID for a wrong document_kind.

Persistence validation emits PERSISTENCE_PRIVATE_DATA_BOUNDARY_INVALID, PERSISTENCE_PROVENANCE_MISSING, and PERSISTENCE_PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION when private-data, provenance, or professional-boundary invariants fail.
Persistence validation emits PERSISTENCE_TELEMETRY_DEFAULT_INVALID when validation_profile.telemetry_default is not 'off'.
Persistence validation recomputes the expected hash and emits PERSISTENCE_PROJECT_HASH_MISMATCH and PERSISTENCE_HASH_MANIFEST_MISMATCH on mismatch.
create_project_store() creates a local SQLite project store and saves the canonical envelope via save_project_store.

open_project_store() opens a local SQLite store, returns its canonical envelope, validates it, and emits PERSISTENCE_STORE_MISSING / PERSISTENCE_STORE_PAYLOAD_MISSING / PERSISTENCE_STORE_HASH_MISMATCH diagnostics.
save_project_store() saves canonical envelope bytes into a local SQLite store, recomputing physical_container, sidecars, and hash, and aborts if any diagnostic is blocking.

completeness_checker crate (DEL-06-03): bounded implementation slice that checks declarative rule-pack required-input declarations against caller-supplied input evidence and reports whether a user rule check is blocked by missing or unreviewed data.

The completeness checker scope covers required-input declarations carrying source kind, required-for intent, dimension and unit requirements (using the PKG-02 canonical dimension vocabulary), provenance requirements, and redistribution requirements.
Scope includes user input evidence records capturing private/user-supplied values, units, dimensions, provenance, redistribution status, and review status.

Scope includes deterministic findings for missing required values, missing units, dimension mismatch, provenance gaps, redistribution gaps, protected-content suspicion, review gaps, duplicate declarations, and unexpected inputs.
Scope includes a rule-check readiness result that maps blocking findings to RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE without changing the mechanics solve status.

The completeness-checker crate does not evaluate formulas, parse rule packs, store private rule data, provide code-specific values, import protected standards content, make professional/code-compliance claims, or generate human acceptance records.
Callers own schema parsing, private storage, unit conversion, expression evaluation, GUI presentation, report rendering, and final result-envelope integration.

Completeness-checker unit tests cover complete invented input evidence, missing values, missing units, dimension mismatch, provenance and redistribution gaps, protected-content suspicions, review gaps, duplicate declarations, unexpected supplied values, reporting-only inputs, and absence of professional/code-compliance statuses.

Crate open_pipe_stress_expression_evaluator (version 0.1.0, edition 2021) is a sandboxed declarative rule-pack expression evaluator for OpenPipeStress and is not published.

The expression evaluator is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-06-02; it evaluates a declarative expression tree supplied by governed rule-pack/application boundaries and does not parse arbitrary text, execute host-language code, load plugins, access files, access the network, spawn processes, provide protected standards content, or make code-compliance claims.

Per human ruling DEC-022 (D-02 Option A, 2026-06-11), the typed AST in this crate is the frozen canonical rule-pack expression grammar (expression_language: open_pipe_stress_declared_expression), versioned by GRAMMAR_VERSION 1.0.0; a writable text syntax is deferred to follow-up ruling D-02b and no parser exists at this freeze.
Frozen v1.0.0 scope: numeric literals and explicit variable bindings carrying dimension and unit-reference metadata.

Frozen scope: arithmetic add/subtract/multiply/divide/negate/abs with enumerated dimension-product algebra over the closed Dimension enum, resolving products/quotients only through the in-crate DIMENSION_PRODUCTS table; unrepresentable or ambiguous results are blocking findings, never silent enum extension.

Derived unit references are composed deterministically (a*b sorted for products, a/b for quotients, ratio for dimensionless); the crate owns no unit conversion, which DEC-018 places at the units-catalog boundary.
Frozen scope: the six comparisons over compatible dimensions with matching unit references.
Frozen scope: boolean and/or/not and the eager select conditional, where all subexpressions are always evaluated and diagnostics in unselected branches block.
Frozen scope: n-ary min/max over same-dimension, same-unit quantities.
Frozen scope: piecewise-linear interpolate and exact/step lookup over user-supplied monotone tables; out-of-range arguments are blocking diagnostics with no extrapolation and no clamping, ever.

Grammar-version gating: the rule pack's declared grammar_version (semver, bound inside the JCS-hashed rule-pack checksum payload) must be in SUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSIONS, else evaluation blocks with UnsupportedGrammarVersion.

The evaluator emits deterministic findings, in fixed evaluation order, for unsafe constructs, unsupported expression forms, missing variables, duplicate bindings, invalid references, non-finite values, division by zero, missing unit metadata, unit mismatches, dimension mismatches, type mismatches, missing required values, malformed tables, out-of-range/missed table lookups, unsupported grammar versions, and analysis-status boundary violations.
The evaluator preserves analysis statuses for mechanics-solved, rule-input-incomplete, user-rule-checked, user-rule-failed, and human-review-required states.
The evaluator accepts structured expression data only; interpolation/lookup mechanisms are public but table values are user value-slots and never repository content.
power and sqrt are excluded from v1.0.0 and recorded as a named open candidate for v1.1 (DEC-022).

The evaluator crate does not implement the required-input completeness checker, private rule-pack lifecycle, checksum handling, public example rule packs, GUI editors, report generation, public API transport, private storage, unit conversion constants, or final result-envelope integration.
Same-dimension arithmetic and comparisons require matching unit references because this crate does not own unit conversion.

In-crate unit tests cover the full function set, dimension algebra (including ambiguity blocking and product-table key uniqueness), grammar version gating, table diagnostics (including non-finite rows JSON cannot encode), eager-select semantics, and pre-freeze behaviors (sandbox refusals, status boundary, binding diagnostics).

The blessed golden conformance corpus fixtures/rule_expressions/conformance_corpus/ (69 cases, invented values only) runs via tests/conformance_corpus.rs under plain cargo test with an enforced coverage floor: every function kind has an accepting case and every relevant finding code has a blocking case; the corpus is the freeze artifact and grammar changes require a corpus extension and version bump.

Module doc: the evaluator crate evaluates explicit expression trees and does not parse text, execute host-language code, access files, access the network, spawn processes, load plugins, embed protected standards content, or emit professional/code-compliance claims.

Grammar freeze (DEC-022 / D-02 Option A): the typed AST is the canonical rule-pack expression grammar frozen at GRAMMAR_VERSION; no text syntax exists at this freeze (deferred to ruling D-02b) and the golden conformance corpus is the freeze artifact.

GRAMMAR_VERSION constant is "1.0.0"; the declared grammar_version sits inside the JCS-canonicalized payload hashed by rule_pack_checksum, so the checksum binds the grammar version, minor versions are additive-only, and breaking changes require a new major version and recorded human ruling.
SUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSIONS constant is the slice ["1.0.0"]; a declared version outside this set produces a blocking UnsupportedGrammarVersion finding rather than best-effort evaluation.
grammar_version_supported(version) returns true when version exactly matches an entry in SUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSIONS.
The evaluator declares its own Dimension enum (closed canonical dimension vocabulary) used for expression typing.
AnalysisStatus enum enumerates the analysis statuses the evaluator preserves across evaluation.
BindingSource enum classifies the origin of a variable binding (e.g., solver result vs user-supplied value).
Quantity struct represents a value with dimension and unit-reference metadata; Quantity::new validates inputs and Quantity::dimensionless builds a dimensionless quantity.
VariableBinding struct binds a variable_id to a source and quantity; VariableBinding::new and VariableBinding::missing construct present and missing bindings.
UnaryOperator enum is Negate, Abs, Not.
BinaryOperator enum is Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide.
LogicalOperator enum is And, Or.
AggregateFunction enum is Min, Max.

LookupMode enum is Exact (argument must exactly equal a row argument; in-range misses are blocking TableKeyNotFound) and Step (largest row argument <= lookup argument applies; out-of-range arguments are blocking TableOutOfRange, never clamped).
TableRow struct is one user-supplied table row with an argument and result f64; values are user value-slots, not repository content.

UserTable struct holds table_id, argument_dimension, argument_unit_ref, result_dimension, result_unit_ref, and rows; row arguments must be strictly increasing and out-of-range arguments are blocking (no extrapolation, no clamping).
ComparisonOperator enum is LessThan, LessThanOrEqual, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, Equal, NotEqual.
Expression enum is the typed AST: Literal, VariableRef, Unary, Binary, Compare, Logical, Select, Aggregate, Interpolate, Lookup, UnsupportedForm, and UnsafeHostAccess.
Logical expressions evaluate eagerly: both operands are always evaluated so diagnostics in either operand always surface.

Select is an eager conditional evaluating condition, then-branch, and else-branch in fixed order so diagnostics in the unselected branch still block; branches must both be booleans or both quantities of the same dimension with matching unit references.
Aggregate computes n-ary min/max over same-dimension, same-unit quantities, evaluating operands left to right with at least one operand required.

Interpolate performs piecewise-linear interpolation over a user-supplied monotone table of at least two rows; arguments outside the closed row-argument range are blocking findings (no extrapolation, no clamping).
Lookup performs exact or step lookup over a user-supplied monotone table.
EvaluationValue enum is either a Quantity or a Boolean.

FindingCode enum enumerates evaluator finding codes: UnsafeConstruct, UnsupportedExpressionForm, MissingVariable, DuplicateBinding, InvalidReference, MissingRequiredValue, NonFiniteInput, DivisionByZero, UnitMetadataMissing, UnitMismatch, DimensionMismatch, TypeMismatch, StatusBoundaryViolation, UnsupportedGrammarVersion, TableMalformed, TableOutOfRange, and TableKeyNotFound.

UnsupportedGrammarVersion finding is always blocking (RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR class); the evaluator never falls back to best-effort evaluation on a missing, malformed, or unsupported declared grammar version.
EvaluationFinding struct records a finding (code, severity, subject, message) produced during evaluation.
EvaluationInput struct carries the expression, variable bindings, current statuses, and the rule pack's declared grammar_version, which must be in SUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSIONS or evaluation blocks.
EvaluationResult struct holds the evaluation outcome; is_blocked reports whether evaluation was blocked.
EvaluationError enum models internal value-construction errors (e.g., non-finite input) used by Quantity construction.
evaluate(input) is the public entry point: it checks grammar version, builds the binding map, validates required variables, evaluates the expression, and collects statuses into an EvaluationResult.
build_binding_map indexes variable bindings by id and emits a blocking DuplicateBinding finding for repeated variable ids.
check_required_variables verifies that referenced variables are bound and emits MissingVariable/MissingRequiredValue findings as appropriate.
eval_expression recursively evaluates an Expression node, dispatching to unary, binary, compare, logical, select, aggregate, and table handlers.
eval_select evaluates condition, then-branch, and else-branch eagerly so diagnostics in the unselected branch still surface and block.
eval_aggregate evaluates n-ary min/max over same-dimension same-unit operands left to right.
validate_table pushes findings in fixed order (id, unit metadata, row count, per-row finiteness, monotonicity) to keep the diagnostic stream deterministic.

eval_table_expression is the shared path for Interpolate (mode None) and Lookup (mode Some): table structure is validated first, then the argument is evaluated, with findings surfacing in that fixed order.

DIMENSION_PRODUCTS is the enumerated dimension-product table over the closed Dimension enum; each commutative (factor_a, factor_b, product) entry defines a unit-free dimensional mechanics relation, and products not in the table are blocking UnsupportedExpressionForm findings with no silent enum extension or fallback to Tbd.

DIMENSION_PRODUCTS encodes mechanics relations including Length*Length=Area, Area*Length=Volume, Force*Length=Moment, Pressure*Area=Force, Stress*Area=Force, Mass*Acceleration=Force, and Density*Volume=Mass.

DIMENSION_PRODUCTS further encodes MassPerLength*Length=Mass, VolumePerLength*Length=Volume, LinearStiffness*Length=Force, LinearStiffness*Displacement=Force, RotationalStiffness*Angle=Moment, and RotationalStiffness*Rotation=Moment.

DIMENSION_PRODUCTS further encodes Stress*SectionModulus=Moment, SectionModulus*Length=SecondMomentArea, Velocity*Time=Length, Acceleration*Time=Velocity, and ThermalExpansionCoefficient*TemperatureInterval=Dimensionless.
dimension_product(left, right) resolves the commutative product of two non-dimensionless dimensions against the enumerated DIMENSION_PRODUCTS table, returning None when unrepresentable.

DimensionQuotient enum represents quotient resolution, including an Ambiguous case when more than one enumerated dimension satisfies candidate x denominator = numerator (the closed enum keeps Pressure and Stress distinct).
dimension_quotient(numerator, denominator) resolves division by inverting DIMENSION_PRODUCTS, finding the unique dimension c with c x denominator = numerator.

derived_product_unit_ref composes the canonical unit reference for a product: dimensionless results reuse the ratio token, otherwise operand unit refs are joined with * in lexicographic byte order so multiplication stays commutative; refs are composed, never converted.
derived_quotient_unit_ref composes the canonical unit reference for a quotient as numerator_ref/denominator_ref (order-preserving).
multiply combines two quantities using dimension_product and derived_product_unit_ref, blocking when the product is unrepresentable.
divide combines two quantities using dimension_quotient and derived_quotient_unit_ref, emitting DivisionByZero and ambiguity findings as needed.
eval_compare evaluates the six comparison operators over compatible-dimension, matching-unit quantities.
check_grammar_version emits a blocking UnsupportedGrammarVersion finding when the declared version is missing, malformed, or not supported.
is_semver enforces strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: three dot-separated decimal components, no signs, no leading zeros, and no pre-release/build suffixes.
collect_statuses gathers preserved analysis statuses from the evaluation input into the result.
quantity_has_required_metadata checks that a quantity carries the unit metadata required for evaluation.
quantity_units_match returns whether two quantities share matching unit references.
validate_finite returns an EvaluationError when a value is not finite, preventing NaN/inf from entering quantities.
conformance_corpus.rs is the golden conformance corpus runner for the frozen rule-pack expression grammar (DEC-022 / D-02 Option A, tranche TP-C1-GRAMMAR-001).

The corpus runner executes every case_*.json file under fixtures/rule_expressions/conformance_corpus/ through evaluate and asserts the recorded expected outcome exactly: value (exact f64 equality on canonical outputs), ordered (code, subject_id) findings, resulting statuses, and sorted source variable ids.
The corpus is the freeze artifact for grammar version GRAMMAR_VERSION: a grammar change without a corresponding corpus extension fails review.

The corpus JSON reader is a test-harness-only strict panic-on-malformed ASCII JSON subset with no dependencies; the evaluator crate itself still does not parse text since rule-pack expressions reach it as structured ASTs.
Corpus boundary: all corpus data is invented (PUBLIC_DOMAIN_OR_ORIGINAL) with no protected standards content and no compliance/certification/approval claims.

REQUIRED_ACCEPT_FEATURES enforces a coverage floor requiring every grammar feature (literals, variable_ref, all unary/binary/compare/logical operators, select, aggregate min/max, interpolate, lookup exact/step) to appear in at least one accepting finding-free case.

REQUIRED_BLOCK_CODES enforces that every relevant finding code appears in at least one blocking case; NonFiniteInput is excluded because finite JSON cannot encode NaN/inf and is pinned by in-crate unit tests instead.

Crate open_pipe_stress_rule_check_runner (version 0.1.0, edition 2021) provides end-to-end rule-check orchestration (C4): completeness, frozen-grammar formula decode and evaluation, ratio-vs-limit acceptability composition, per-check status, and worst-of aggregation over a rule-pack document plus caller-resolved solver and user values, with no text parsing, network/host/filesystem access, protected content, or compliance claims.
rule_check_runner depends on open_pipe_stress_expression_evaluator, open_pipe_stress_completeness_checker, open_pipe_stress_rule_pack_document, open_pipe_stress_units, serde, and serde_json.
Crate rule_check_runner provides end-to-end rule-check orchestration for user-owned rule packs (completion plan C4 — end-to-end rule checks on authored models).

The runner wires three engine crates into one runnable path: the completeness checker (required inputs present), the rule_pack_document codec (decode the frozen-grammar formula AST), and the expression evaluator (compute the formula and the acceptability comparison).
Per check, the runner produces one of three automatic rule-check statuses — RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, USER_RULE_CHECKED, USER_RULE_FAILED — and aggregates them worst-of.

The runner is pure in-memory orchestration: it does not parse text, execute host-language code, access files or network, spawn processes, load plugins, store private data, embed protected standards content, or emit professional/certification/sealing/authentication/approval/code-compliance claims.
Acceptability composition: a check whose formula evaluates to a boolean uses that boolean directly as the acceptability predicate.

A check whose formula evaluates to a quantity (e.g. a ratio) is compared against the single user-supplied limit named by the check's value_slot_refs, via a synthesized Compare(formula, relation, limit) evaluated through the same evaluator.

Before the evaluator boundary, B2/B3 unit normalization converts compatible DEC-018 catalog units to the declaration's unit; exact non-catalog demonstration units remain valid only when entered and declared unit strings match; incompatible or unknown unit substitutions block rather than evaluating.

The acceptability relation is the check's optional acceptability_relation member (TP-C4-ACCEPTREL-001), one of four ordering relations less_than/less_than_or_equal/greater_than/greater_than_or_equal, defaulting to less_than_or_equal when absent (backward compatible).

An explicit but unrecognized acceptability_relation token blocks the check rather than defaulting silently; the member is an additive PROPOSAL awaiting human ratification, and equality acceptance is a deliberate non-goal.
Input binding is a C4-defined minimal mechanism: the schema carries no selector tying a solver_result required input to a solved result row, so the binding is caller-supplied.
Solver values are supplied via SolverResultBinding (caller extracts {value, unit} for an input_id from a solved mechanics envelope); user values and limit slots via SuppliedValueBinding.

private_library_value inputs are resolved via LibraryValueBinding (C3 rule-pack/library reference wiring): the caller reads {value, unit} from the referenced private library record's value slot named by the rule pack's library_value_ref member in the local store.

A private_library_value input with no resolved library binding stays unsupplied (never a silent pass) with a recorded note; the library value is resolved at run time and never embedded in the rule pack (IP boundary).
DOCUMENT_KIND is the document-kind tag on a serialized run result: 'openpipestress.rule_check.run'.

PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY_NOTICE is carried on every run result: software rule-check evidence only; not a professional, certification, sealing, authentication, approval, or code-compliance claim; human review remains required.
Struct SolverResultBinding represents one solver value the caller resolved from a solved mechanics envelope for a solver_result required input (fields input_id, result_id, value, unit).

Struct SuppliedValueBinding represents one user-entered value for a user_supplied_rule_value required input or a value_slot limit; dimension is the snake_case dimension token (fields ref_id, value, unit, dimension).

Struct LibraryValueBinding represents one value the caller resolved from a saved private library for a private_library_value required input; the value is never embedded in the rule pack and stays in the private library (IP boundary).

Struct RuleCheckRunInput carries inputs to a rule-check run: rule_pack_document, solver_results, supplied_values, library_values, and current analysis statuses; the caller is expected to have already run document validation.

Enum RuleCheckStatus is the three automatic rule-check statuses the runner may emit (RuleInputsIncomplete, UserRuleChecked, UserRuleFailed); MODEL_INCOMPLETE, MECHANICS_SOLVED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, and HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT are intentionally not producible here.
RuleCheckStatus::as_str maps each status variant to its canonical screaming-snake-case string token.
RuleCheckStatus::severity_rank defines worst-of precedence: failed (2) > incomplete (1) > checked (0).
Struct ComputedQuantity is a computed or limit quantity surfaced in a check outcome (fields value, dimension, unit_ref).
Struct BoundInput records what a single rule-pack input resolved to for a check (input_id, source_kind, supplied flag, optional value/unit/result_id/note).
Struct RunFinding is a finding surfaced from completeness or evaluation, traced to its engine (fields code, severity, subject_id, message).

Struct CheckOutcome is the outcome of one check_definition, carrying check_id, status, optional computed_value and limit_value, the governing acceptability_relation, bound_inputs, completeness/evaluator findings, and diagnostic_codes.
Struct RuleCheckRunResult is the result of a run over all of a pack's checks (document_kind, rule_pack_id, grammar_version, aggregate_status, checks, professional_boundary_notice).
Function run_rule_checks runs every check_definition in the rule pack against the caller-resolved values and returns per-check outcomes plus a worst-of aggregate.
run_rule_checks collects per-check outcomes by mapping run_one_check over the document's check_definitions array.
When a pack has no checks, the aggregate status is RuleInputsIncomplete; otherwise it is the worst-of reduction over each check's status by severity_rank.

Struct RunContext holds the per-run indices (required_inputs, value_slots, formula_declarations) and the caller-supplied binding maps (solver_by_input, supplied_by_ref, library_by_input) plus current_statuses and grammar_version.
Struct ResolvedValue is a value resolved for a required input, ready to bind into the evaluator (value, unit, eval_dimension, binding_source).

Function run_one_check resolves a single check: its check_id, declared result_statuses, and diagnostic_policy, then resolves required inputs, runs completeness, decodes and evaluates the formula, and composes acceptability.

When a check references an input id absent from the required_index, run_one_check pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE completeness finding ('check references an undeclared required input') and skips it.

Each required input's supplied value is resolved per source kind: SolverResult from solver_by_input, PrivateLibraryValue from library_by_input, UserSuppliedRuleValue from supplied_by_ref, and any other kind falls back to supplied_by_ref.
A resolved private_library_value records a provenance note naming the library kind/id, record, and slot, and states the value stays in the private library and is never embedded in the rule pack.
An unresolved private_library_value records a note that it has no resolved library reference (missing library_value_ref or the library/record/slot was not found) and is treated as unsupplied.
Each supplied value is normalized to the declared unit via normalize_value_to_declared_unit; a normalization error pushes an evaluator finding and leaves the value/unit unset.
A supplied value with a known dimension passes the completeness gates via the private-reviewed constructor; otherwise the input is left unsupplied so completeness blocks (never a silent pass).
run_one_check runs check_completeness over the assembled required and supplied inputs plus the current statuses, mapping each completeness finding into a RunFinding.

If completeness readiness is Blocked or any blocking completeness finding exists, the check returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a missing_input diagnostic and acceptability_relation 'none', without evaluating the formula.
The formula is resolved from the formula_index by the check's formula_ref ref_id; an undeclared formula pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE finding and blocks after completeness.
A formula declaration with no declaration_payload.expression_ast pushes a blocking INVALID_REFERENCE finding and blocks after completeness.
The expression AST is decoded via decode_expression; a decode error pushes a blocking DECODE_ERROR finding and blocks after completeness.

The formula's variable references are bound to resolved values; a resolved value with a known eval_dimension binds a Quantity, otherwise it binds a missing VariableBinding (never a silent substitution).

The formula is computed by evaluate over the EvaluationInput (expression, bindings, required_variable_ids, current statuses, declared grammar version); any evaluator finding blocks after completeness.
When the formula evaluates to a Boolean, true yields USER_RULE_CHECKED and false yields USER_RULE_FAILED, with acceptability_relation 'formula_predicate'.

When the formula evaluates to a Quantity, the top-level acceptability relation is resolved (computed relation limit); an unsupported acceptability_relation token pushes a blocking RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR and returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with relation 'none'.

For a quantity check, the limit is resolved via resolve_limit; a resolution error or absent limit returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE (with RULE_INPUT_MISSING when no user-supplied value-slot limit is available).
The limit quantity is built from the limit value, unit, and dimension; missing or unknown unit/dimension metadata pushes a blocking RULE_EVALUATOR_ERROR and returns RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE.

The acceptability comparison evaluates Expression::Compare(operator, formula_quantity, limit_quantity) through the same evaluator; Boolean true yields USER_RULE_CHECKED, false yields USER_RULE_FAILED, otherwise RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE.

Function resolve_limit resolves a check's governing limit from the first value_slot_refs entry, taking the numeric value from the caller's supplied-value map keyed by slot id, and returns (value, unit, eval_dimension).
resolve_limit prefers the value_slot's declared dimension and unit_ref from the value_slot_index, falling back to the binding's dimension/unit, then normalizes the value to the declared unit.

Function normalize_value_to_declared_unit returns the value unchanged when entered and declared unit strings match; missing declared/entered unit metadata or a 'TBD' declared unit yields a blocking UnitMismatch finding.

normalize_value_to_declared_unit resolves the dimension and the entered/declared unit symbols and converts via convert_for_dimension; an unknown dimension, incompatible unit, or failed conversion yields a blocking UnitMismatch finding.
Function unit_mismatch_finding builds a blocking UnitMismatch RunFinding describing that an entered unit cannot be normalized to the declared unit for the given dimension, with a reason.
Function resolve_acceptability_relation resolves a check's acceptability relation (computed relation limit) to a frozen-grammar comparison operator.
An absent acceptability_relation member resolves to LessThanOrEqual, preserving historical behaviour for packs authored before the additive member existed (the sole documented default).
An explicit but unrecognized acceptability_relation token is never silently defaulted; resolve_acceptability_relation returns Err(token) so the caller blocks the check (no-silent-defaults, CONTRACT).
resolve_acceptability_relation maps tokens less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal to their operators; empty string maps to LessThanOrEqual; any other token returns Err.
Function acceptability_relation_label gives the canonical string label for an acceptability relation operator, reported on the check outcome so the GUI shows the governing relation.
Function quantity_to_computed converts an evaluator Quantity into a ComputedQuantity, encoding the dimension to its document token and copying value and unit_ref.
Function blocked_after_completeness returns a RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE CheckOutcome with an evaluator_error diagnostic and acceptability_relation 'none' for checks that block after completeness passed.

Function enforce_declared keeps an emitted status inside the check's declared result_statuses envelope; an undeclared status is downgraded to RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE with a blocking STATUS_NOT_DECLARED finding.
Function push_diagnostic appends a diagnostic code resolved from the check's diagnostic_policy for a given key, de-duplicating already-present codes.
Function index_by builds a HashMap from an array member of the document keyed by each item's id field.

Function source_kind_from_token maps source-kind tokens (solver_result, model_input, user_supplied_rule_value, private_library_value, owner_design_basis) to SourceKind, defaulting unknown tokens to Tbd.
Function required_for_from_token maps required-for tokens (rule_check, reporting, diagnostic) to RequiredFor, defaulting unknown tokens to Tbd.
Function severity_str maps a FindingSeverity (Info, Warning, Blocking) to its lowercase string.
Function to_automatic_status maps an evaluator AnalysisStatus to a completeness AutomaticAnalysisStatus; HumanApprovedForProject maps to HumanReviewRequired.

Function completeness_dimension_from_token maps a snake_case dimension token to the completeness checker's dimension by routing through the document codec's evaluator-dimension decode (single source of truth for the token vocabulary).
Function eval_dimension_to_completeness maps each evaluator Dimension variant to the corresponding completeness Dimension variant.
