Crate open_pipe_stress_rule_pack_document is the rule-pack document seam: production codec between the rule-pack JSON document encoding and the frozen DEC-022 expression AST, JCS checksum computation, and document-level lifecycle validation; no text parsing, no protected content, no compliance claims.
rule_pack_document depends on the expression_evaluator, rule_pack_lifecycle, and canonical_json crates plus serde and serde_json.

Crate rule_pack_document (Phase C2 backend, DEC-022 basis) is the production bridge between rule-pack JSON documents (schemas/rule_pack.schema.yaml) and the frozen expression grammar in the expression evaluator.
The codec maps between the node-tagged JSON expression encoding (pinned by fixtures/rule_expressions/conformance_corpus/) and the evaluator's typed AST.
The crate computes the RFC 8785 (JCS) checksum over a pack document with the checksums member excluded, grammar-version-bound per DEC-022 through the rule_pack_lifecycle crate.
The crate provides document-level validation surfacing lifecycle, grammar, expression, and checksum findings for the desktop editor.

The crate does not parse expression text (a writable text syntax awaits the D-02b human ruling), does not store private payloads, does not choose storage paths, and emits no professional/certification/sealing/authentication/code-compliance claims.

CHECKSUM_PAYLOAD_EXCLUDES is the document member excluded from the canonical checksum payload ('checksums'); the checksum cannot cover itself, and the exclusion is recorded in checksum evidence as payload_excludes.
CHECKSUM_BASIS is the stable label for how rule-pack document checksums are computed: 'rfc8785_jcs_sha256_excluding_checksums'.

DIMENSION_TOKENS is the canonical mapping between snake_case document dimension tokens and the evaluator Dimension enum (dimensionless, length, mass, time, temperature, stress, pressure, moment, etc., plus TBD).
Function decode_dimension decodes a snake_case dimension token from the document vocabulary into a Dimension, or None when unknown.
Function encode_dimension encodes an evaluator Dimension as its document token (every Dimension variant has a token).
Struct DecodeError is a decode failure with a JSON-path-style breadcrumb (path, message) for editor diagnostics.
Helper object() requires a JSON value to be an object, returning a DecodeError otherwise.
Helper member() fetches a required map member, returning a DecodeError 'missing required member' otherwise.
Helper string_member()/number_member() fetch a required member as a string or finite number, returning a DecodeError on type mismatch.
Helper optional_bool() reads an optional boolean member with a default.
Function decode_quantity decodes a quantity object (value, dimension, unit_ref, optional unit_required and dimension_check_required defaulting true); an unknown dimension token is a DecodeError.

Function decode_table decodes a UserTable (table_id, argument/result dimensions and unit_refs, and rows of argument/result numbers); unknown dimension tokens or a non-array rows member are DecodeErrors.
Function decode_expression decodes a node-tagged JSON expression into the evaluator AST.

decode_expression accepts the full corpus encoding including the evaluator refusal markers unsupported_form / unsafe_host_access, which always evaluate to blocking findings; pack-document validation and the schema additionally reject refusal markers as authorable content.

decode_expression dispatches on the node tag: literal, variable_ref, unary, binary, compare, logical, select, aggregate, interpolate, lookup, unsupported_form, unsafe_host_access; an unknown node kind is a DecodeError.
Unary nodes accept operators negate, abs, not; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Binary nodes accept operators add, subtract, multiply, divide; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Compare nodes accept operators less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, equal, not_equal; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Logical nodes accept operators and, or; an unknown operator is a DecodeError.
Select nodes decode a condition and then/else branches.
Aggregate nodes accept functions min, max over an operands array; an unknown function or non-array operands is a DecodeError.
Interpolate nodes decode a table plus an argument expression.
Lookup nodes accept modes exact, step over a table and an argument; an unknown mode is a DecodeError.
Function encode_expression encodes an evaluator AST back into the node-tagged JSON encoding, the inverse of decode_expression across every node kind.

Function expression_contains_refusal_marker returns true when an expression tree contains an evaluator refusal marker (UnsupportedForm or UnsafeHostAccess); refusal markers are engine vocabulary, never authorable pack content.
Struct DocumentError is a document-level failure (subject, message) that prevents checksum computation or validation.
Function canonical_payload_bytes returns the RFC 8785 canonical byte payload a rule-pack checksum covers: the document with the CHECKSUM_PAYLOAD_EXCLUDES members removed.
Struct ComputedRulePackChecksum is serializable checksum evidence (algorithm, canonicalization, payload_scope, payload_ref, payload_excludes, basis, grammar_version, grammar_version_bound, value).

Function compute_rule_pack_checksum computes the grammar-version-bound JCS checksum of a rule-pack document; the canonicalization label is 'JCS' because the function produces canonical bytes itself via canonical_json (RFC 8785).
compute_rule_pack_checksum requires a rule_pack_id and a top-level grammar_version (DEC-022), returning a DocumentError when either is missing.
Struct ValidationFinding is a document validation finding (code, subject, message, blocking).
Struct FormulaValidation reports per-formula validation (formula_id, declaration_form, decode_status, findings).
Struct ChecksumValidation reports the declared value, recomputed checksum, and a match_status of match | mismatch_review_required | declared_placeholder | not_computable.

Struct RulePackDocumentValidation is the document validation envelope for the desktop editor; statuses describe software findings only and are not professional/certification/sealing/authentication/code-compliance claims.
Function map_privacy_class maps privacy_class tokens (public_schema_only, public_invented_example, private_user_data, private_project_data, quarantined) to PrivacyClass, defaulting to Tbd.

Function map_redistribution_status maps redistribution tokens (public_permissive, private_only, unknown, protected_suspected, invented_non_engineering_example) to RedistributionStatus, defaulting to Tbd.
Function map_review_status maps review_status tokens (pending, accepted, rejected, quarantined) to ReviewStatus, defaulting to Tbd.

The schema's lifecycle_status vocabulary is wider than the crate enum; since validate_lifecycle does not branch on the field, map_lifecycle_status maps unrepresentable tokens to Tbd rather than interpreting them.

Function lifecycle_finding_code maps each lifecycle finding code enum variant to its screaming-snake-case string (e.g. MISSING_GRAMMAR_VERSION, STALE_CHECKSUM, PROTECTED_CONTENT_SUSPECTED, PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY_VIOLATION).
Function is_placeholder_checksum treats an empty or TBD-prefixed (case-insensitive) checksum value as a placeholder.

Function validate_rule_pack_document validates a rule-pack document: shape-critical members, grammar version, every declarative-AST formula payload, lifecycle/privacy/provenance findings, and the recorded checksum against a fresh JCS computation.
Validation requires rule_pack_kind to equal 'open_pipe_stress_rule_pack', pushing a blocking UNEXPECTED_DOCUMENT_KIND finding otherwise.

Validation requires a non-empty, strict-semver, evaluator-supported grammar_version; absence pushes blocking MISSING_GRAMMAR_VERSION and an unsupported version pushes blocking UNSUPPORTED_GRAMMAR_VERSION (evaluation would block, never best-effort).

Validation decodes each declarative_ast formula's expression_ast: a decoded refusal marker pushes blocking REFUSAL_MARKER_AUTHORED, a decode failure pushes blocking EXPRESSION_DECODE_FAILED, and a missing AST pushes blocking MISSING_EXPRESSION_AST.

The rule_pack_lifecycle crate is the bounded implementation slice for DEL-06-04: it records rule-pack lifecycle metadata, privacy/redistribution state, checksum evidence, and audit/report-facing manifest hooks without storing private rule-pack payloads in the public repository.

Scope: rule-pack identity, display name, schema version, rule-pack version, expression grammar version (DEC-022), lifecycle status, source notice, privacy class, redistribution status, review status, and protected-content review flags.

Scope: SHA-256 checksum records over caller-supplied payload bytes, with explicit metadata distinguishing caller-supplied JCS-compatible bytes from JSON canonicalization the crate has actually verified.
Scope: grammar-version checksum binding per DEC-022 — the declared strict-semver grammar_version must sit inside the JCS-hashed rule-pack payload bytes so the FR-016 reported checksum binds it.

The crate provides the exact JCS member encoding (grammar_version_jcs_member), a byte-containment evidence check (payload_declares_grammar_version, a necessary-condition check on caller bytes, not JSON parsing), and a binding-enforcing checksum constructor.

Scope: deterministic lifecycle findings for missing source notices, missing/unknown redistribution state, missing/malformed/unbound grammar versions, missing/stale checksums, suspected protected content, attempted public export of private content, and professional-boundary violations.
Scope: audit-manifest references that expose only identity, version, grammar version, checksum, source notice, and privacy/redistribution metadata.

Boundary: the crate does not parse or canonicalize JSON, implement storage paths, encrypt private rule packs, manage access control, handle secrets, run a GUI, render reports, define API transport, or evaluate engineering/code rules; callers own canonical JSON serialization before hashing.
Boundary: the grammar-version binding check is byte containment over caller-supplied bytes, never JSON parsing; PKG-12 owns storage, access, and secret-handling policy.

Verification: unit tests cover deterministic SHA-256 checksums, unverified caller-supplied JCS-byte metadata, missing-metadata diagnostics, grammar-version findings, the binding-enforcing constructor, private export blocking, protected-content quarantine, stale checksum detection, audit hook redaction, and professional-boundary enforcement.

Verification: the golden checksum-binding corpus fixtures/rule_expressions/checksum_binding/ pins byte/hash stability and the DEC-022 property that changing or removing the grammar_version member changes the rule-pack checksum.

core/rules/rule_pack_lifecycle records metadata and reproducibility evidence for user-owned rule packs; it does not store private payloads, parse/canonicalize JSON, implement encryption/access control, expose private formulas, or make professional/code-compliance claims.

GRAMMAR_VERSION_PAYLOAD_KEY = "grammar_version": the JSON member key binding the expression grammar version inside the JCS-canonicalized rule-pack payload bytes hashed by rule_pack_checksum (DEC-022).
Because the grammar_version member sits inside the hashed bytes, the reported checksum (FR-016) changes whenever the declared grammar version changes.

grammar_version_jcs_member(version) returns the exact JCS encoding of the grammar-version member ("grammar_version":"<version>"); JCS emits sorted keys with no insignificant whitespace, so this byte sequence must appear verbatim in any JCS payload declaring the version at an object boundary.

payload_declares_grammar_version(canonical_payload, grammar_version) is a byte-containment check for the exact JCS member encoding; since the crate does not parse JSON it is a necessary-condition check, and absence is conclusive that the payload cannot bind the declared grammar version.

is_semver_grammar_version(version) enforces strict MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: three dot-separated decimal components, no signs, no leading zeros, no pre-release/build suffixes; it mirrors the evaluator-side rule in core/rules/expression_evaluator.

The Pipe Section Property Calculator (DEL-03-08) implements bounded pipe section and mass-property calculations from user-entered dimensions and densities.

The section calculator is intentionally narrow: it accepts already-parsed values (not external catalog formats), provides no schedule/dimensional/material/component defaults, does not convert units until the project unit catalog is accepted, records blocking diagnostics for missing/non-positive/incompatible inputs, and marks calculated values as derived from user-entered data.

For circular pipe sections the calculator derives effective inside diameter after corrosion allowance, metal area, second moment of area, elastic section modulus, polar/torsional constant, contents volume per length, and metal/contents/insulation/total mass per length when matching density inputs are provided.

Inputs remain user-supplied; public fixtures and schemas must not use this module to smuggle protected dimensional tables, proprietary catalog values, code-specific allowables, SIFs, flexibility factors, or private project data into the repository.

core/section_properties/calculator.py computes pipe section and mass properties from user-entered values; it provides no dimensional tables, material defaults, unit-conversion constants, or catalog lookups, requires explicit compatible unit metadata, and reports diagnostics when inputs are insufficient.
calculator.py constants: LENGTH_DIMENSIONS={"length"}, DENSITY_DIMENSIONS={"density"}, DIAGNOSTIC_SOURCE="core/section_properties/calculator.py".
Quantity is a frozen dataclass with magnitude (float), unit (str), dimension (str), and provenance (dict).
SectionDiagnostic is a frozen dataclass with code, diagnostic_class, severity, field, source, affected_object, message, remediation, provenance.
PipeSectionInput frozen dataclass: outside_diameter and wall_thickness (Quantity|None) plus optional corrosion_allowance, material_density, contents_density, insulation_thickness, insulation_density.
PipeSectionResult frozen dataclass holds properties dict and diagnostics tuple; its accepted property is true when no diagnostic has blocking severity.

calculate_pipe_section_properties computes pipe section properties using explicit compatible units only, validating required and optional quantities and returning early with diagnostics if any are present.
calculate_pipe_section_properties enforces a single shared length unit across outside_diameter, wall_thickness, corrosion_allowance, and insulation_thickness inputs.
calculate_pipe_section_properties enforces a single (optional) density unit across material, contents, and insulation densities.
effective_wall = wall.magnitude - corrosion_value, and inside_diameter = od.magnitude - 2*effective_wall.
The calculator emits SECTION_CALCULATION_INPUT_INVALID when corrosion allowance leaves no positive effective wall, when inside diameter is negative, or when insulation thickness is negative.

Section geometry formulas: metal_area = pi/4*(OD^2 - ID^2); moment_of_inertia = pi/64*(OD^4 - ID^4); section_modulus = I/(OD/2); torsional_constant = pi/32*(OD^4 - ID^4); contents_volume_per_length = pi/4*ID^2.

The properties dict carries inside_diameter, metal_area, cross_section_area, moment_of_inertia (unit length^4), section_modulus (length^3), torsional_constant (length^4), and contents_volume_per_length (length^2) as Quantity values with dimension labels.

Mass-per-length parts are computed only when a density unit is present: metal_mass = metal_area*material_density; contents_mass = contents_volume_per_length*contents_density; insulation_mass = insulation_area*insulation_density.
Insulation outside diameter = OD + 2*insulation_thickness and insulation_area = pi/4*(insulation_OD^2 - OD^2).
When mass parts exist, each is given unit density_unit*length^2 with dimension mass_per_length and a total mass_per_length is added as their sum.

quantity_from_mapping builds a Quantity from schema-like value metadata (unit/unit_ref, dimension/dimension_id, magnitude, provenance), returning None if it is not a dict or any required field is missing.
_require_quantity emits SECTION_DIMENSION_MISSING for a None required field, otherwise validates the quantity.
_optional_quantity returns None for absent optional fields, otherwise validates the quantity.

_validate_quantity emits SECTION_UNIT_MISSING (empty unit/dimension), SECTION_PROVENANCE_MISSING (no provenance), SECTION_DIMENSION_INCONSISTENT (dimension not in expected), and SECTION_CALCULATION_INPUT_INVALID for non-positive or negative values (corrosion_allowance and insulation_thickness exempt from the positive check).

_single_unit returns the shared unit of present quantities, emitting SECTION_DIMENSION_INCONSISTENT for mismatched units (the calculator does not convert units in this deliverable) and SECTION_UNIT_MISSING when a required unit is empty.

Crate open_pipe_stress_canonical_json provides RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON serialization shared by every OpenPipeStress hash seam.
canonical_json depends on serde_json and ryu, using ryu for ECMAScript-equal shortest round-trip float rendering because the std formatter breaks ties differently.
Crate canonical_json is the single canonical-JSON text authority (completion-plan row H5, DEC-010 JCS-compatible hashing baseline) so every JSON-hashing surface renders identical canonical bytes.
RFC 8785 conformance: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units (§3.2.3); strings escaped exactly as ECMAScript JSON.stringify (§3.2.2.2) via serde_json.
Numbers render in ECMAScript Number::toString shortest round-trip decimal form (§3.2.2.3) with -0 rendered as 0; digit selection comes from ryu (closest shortest candidate, ties to even).

One documented divergence: serde_json preserves i64/u64 integers exactly, so integers beyond 2^53 keep full precision rather than collapsing to the nearest IEEE double; such values cannot arrive distinct through a JavaScript lane since JSON.parse rounds first.
canonical_json(value: &Value) -> String renders a JSON value as RFC 8785 canonical JSON text.
write_canonical emits null/true/false literals, numbers via canonical_number, strings via serde_json, arrays in order, and objects with keys sorted by UTF-16 code units.
Per RFC 8785 §3.2.3, property names sort as arrays of UTF-16 code units (ECMAScript string comparison), not as Unicode code points, which differ for supplementary-plane keys.
canonical_number renders integer-repr numbers via serde's exact rendering and float-repr numbers via the ECMAScript Number::toString algorithm.
ecma_number_to_string implements ECMAScript Number::toString (ECMA-262 §6.1.6.1.20, radix 10) for finite doubles, asserting the value is finite and rendering -0 as 0.

ecma_number_to_string sources shortest round-trip digits from ryu, which selects the same digit string ECMAScript engines do; the std formatter diverged in 7 of 20k random doubles and cannot be the digit source.

ECMA-262 notation expresses value = s x 10^(n-k), where s is the k-digit shortest integer significand and n positions the decimal point; branches cover integer, fractional, leading-zero, and exponential forms (plain decimal for n in (-7,21], else exponential).
shortest_digits extracts the significand digits (no leading/trailing zeros) and the decimal exponent of the first digit from a ryu-rendered positive finite float.
Test rfc8785_appendix_b_bit_pattern_vectors verifies 13 RFC 8785 Appendix B bit-pattern vectors against node JSON.stringify (verified 2026-06-11).
Test ecma_notation_branch_vectors verifies 16 literal vectors across every ECMAScript notation branch against node JSON.stringify (verified 2026-06-11).
Test float_and_integer_repr_converge confirms float-repr (200.0), integer-repr (200), and in-process f64 values render the same canonical bytes.
Test integers_beyond_2_53_keep_exact_precision confirms u64/i64 integers beyond 2^53 keep exact precision (outside the I-JSON envelope).
Test objects_sort_keys_by_utf16_code_units confirms keys sort by UTF-16 code units so a surrogate-pair key precedes a BMP key, unlike code-point order.
Test strings_escape_exactly_as_json_stringify confirms two-character escapes where defined, lowercase \u00xx for other control characters, and literal non-ASCII characters (RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2).
Test composite_document_matches_ecmascript_rendering pins a composite document against node JSON.stringify(sortedDeep(value)) output.

Scope: deterministic diagnostics from sparse LDLᵀ factorization reports, including a NonPositivePivot warning with count and first location when the reduced stiffness is not positive definite.
Scope: mapping linear support findings/application errors and primitive load findings into diagnostic records, with stable affected references for primitive-load missing-ID findings.

The frame kernel crate is the conservative first slice for DEL-04-01, providing a code-neutral mechanics kernel for 3D Euler-Bernoulli frame stiffness, coordinate transforms, boundary-condition reduction, global dense assembly, and a temporary dense solve interface.
Frame kernel scope: two-node 3D frame elements with six degrees of freedom per node, plus public node and element DOF mapping helpers for the fixed six-DOF ordering.
The kernel provides local 12-by-12 Euler-Bernoulli stiffness terms for axial, torsion, bending about local y, and bending about local z.

The kernel provides direction-cosine transforms from validated local element axes to global axes, and dense global assembly with boundary-condition reduction including force adjustment for prescribed displacements.
The kernel uses deterministic dense Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting for small reduced systems.
Each node uses the deterministic six-DOF ordering [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz].

For an element, node i occupies DOF indices 0..6 and node j occupies indices 6..12; external slices should bind this ordering via node_dof_index, element_dof_map, FrameDof, and NODE_DOF_ORDER rather than re-deriving offsets.

The dense matrix and dense solve functions are interim interfaces suitable only for focused kernel verification and small tests; the project sparse solver strategy is resolved by DEC-023 as the in-repo skyline LDL^T direct solver, with the dense path serving as the parity oracle. This crate introduces no external numerical dependency.

Inputs to the crate are numeric mechanics quantities that upstream schema and unit layers must already have validated for unit compatibility; the crate validates finite, positive, nondegenerate, orientation, node-index, boundary-condition, and singular-system conditions but does not define the project unit catalog, conversion constants, or solver tolerance policy.
The dense solve path has an internal zero-pivot guard for temporary verification behavior; that guard is not a release tolerance policy, conditioning policy, or sparse-solver selection.

Solver-facing external boundaries must bind raw mechanics fields to FrameKernelUnitBasis metadata before schema, service, adapter, report, or persistence use; the unit basis carries caller-supplied unit identifiers for length, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, and rotation, performs no conversion, and supplies no defaults.
Optional CanonicalModelReference records bind solver object references to PKG-02 model roles without changing the mechanics kernel.

The shared CanonicalDimension metadata vocabulary exposes force_per_length for downstream solver/load boundaries labeling distributed mechanics quantities; the frame kernel records the dimension identifier only and defines no unit catalog, conversion constants, load defaults, or tolerance policy.

Non-compliance boundary: the frame kernel computes open mechanics quantities only and does not encode compliance rules, code-specific values, protected standard content, material allowables, SIF/flexibility data, private project data, or engineering approval/certification claims.

Frame kernel verification: unit tests cover six-DOF mapping, local stiffness terms, local-to-global transform behavior, global assembly, boundary-condition reduction, prescribed-displacement force adjustment, the temporary dense solve interface, singular-system detection, metadata boundaries, invalid node topology, repeated restraints, invalid orientation, and non-finite input rejection.

The intended future replacement boundary is the reduced-system solve interface; element stiffness, transforms, assembly, and reduction can be preserved while replacing solve_dense with an accepted sparse solver adapter.
The frame kernel crate contains open mechanics routines only; it does not encode design-code compliance checks, protected standards content, or private project data.
Frame kernel DOF constants: DOF_PER_NODE=6, NODES_PER_ELEMENT=2, ELEMENT_DOF=12, with local DOF indices UX=0, UY=1, UZ=2, RX=3, RY=4, RZ=5.
AXIS_TOLERANCE is 1.0e-12; DENSE_SOLVE_ZERO_PIVOT_GUARD is 1.0e-12 and is an internal dense verification pivot guard, not the project solver tolerance policy.
Frame kernel type aliases: Matrix3 is 3x3, Matrix12 is ELEMENT_DOF x ELEMENT_DOF, DenseMatrix is Vec<Vec<f64>>, DenseVector is Vec<f64>.
FrameDof enum names the six local degrees of freedom Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz, with local_index, as_str, and is_translational helpers.
FrameDof::is_translational is true for Ux, Uy, and Uz.
NODE_DOF_ORDER is the fixed array [Ux, Uy, Uz, Rx, Ry, Rz] of length DOF_PER_NODE.
node_dof_index computes a global DOF index as node_index * DOF_PER_NODE + dof.local_index().
element_dof_map returns the 12-entry global DOF index map for an element, with node i in the first six entries and node j in the next six.

CanonicalDimension enum enumerates the shared metadata dimension vocabulary including length, force, moment, pressure, stress, area, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, second_moment_area, force_per_length, slope, and TBD.
CanonicalDimension::as_str returns the canonical string identifier for each dimension (e.g. LinearStiffness -> 'linear_stiffness', Tbd -> 'TBD').
UnitSystemRef wraps a non-empty, non-TBD unit_system_id; its constructor returns None for blank or 'TBD' values.
QuantityUnitMetadata pairs a normalized unit_id with a CanonicalDimension and exposes dimension_id.
FrameKernelUnitBasis binds a unit system reference plus unit metadata for coordinate, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, and rotation quantities.
FrameKernelUnitBasis::new accepts the unit basis only if has_expected_dimensions passes, ensuring each unit's CanonicalDimension matches its expected role.

FrameKernelUnitBasis::from_unit_ids constructs the basis from string unit IDs, attaching the expected CanonicalDimension to each (length, force, moment, stress, area, second_moment_area, displacement, rotation).
FrameKernelUnitBasis::has_expected_dimensions verifies each unit's dimension equals its required canonical dimension.
CanonicalModelRole enum distinguishes PhysicalSourceOfTruth from AnalyticalSolverModel, with string forms 'physical_source_of_truth' and 'analytical_solver_model'.
CanonicalModelReference binds a model_id, model_role, and object_ref; its constructor rejects blank or TBD identifiers.
normalize_explicit_id trims a value and returns None if it is empty or case-insensitively equal to 'TBD', otherwise the trimmed string.

FrameKernelError enum enumerates validation failures: NonFiniteInput, NonPositiveInput, DegenerateAxis, InvalidOrientation, InvalidNodeIndex, RepeatedElementNodeIndex, InvalidMatrixDimensions, InvalidVectorLength, RepeatedRestrainedDof, RestrainedDofOutOfRange, RepeatedPrescribedDof, PrescribedDofOutOfRange, and SingularSystem.
FrameNode holds an index and 3D coordinates; its constructor validates that coordinates are finite.
FrameSection holds elastic_modulus, shear_modulus, area, second_moment_y, second_moment_z, and torsion_constant; its constructor requires all to be positive and finite.
FrameProperties pairs a FrameSection with a positive finite length.
FrameOrientation stores local unit axes (rows x, y, z) expressed in global coordinates.
FrameOrientation::new validates each axis is finite and unit length, requires mutual orthogonality within AXIS_TOLERANCE, and requires a right-handed basis (cross(x,y) equals z).
FrameOrientation::from_x_axis_and_y_reference builds an orthonormal basis by normalizing the local x axis, Gram-Schmidt projecting the y reference, and taking z as the cross product.
FrameOrientation::transformation_matrix builds a 12x12 transform by copying the 3x3 rotation block onto each node's translational and rotational DOF blocks.
FrameElement holds node_i, node_j, section, and a y_reference vector; its constructor rejects an element connecting a node to itself and validates properties and orientation.
FrameElement::length returns the Euclidean distance between node coordinates (after validating the direction is non-degenerate).
FrameElement::local_stiffness and global_stiffness compute the element local stiffness and then transform it to global coordinates via the element orientation.
ReducedSystem holds the reduced stiffness matrix, reduced force vector, and the list of free (unconstrained) DOFs.
local_stiffness computes the 12x12 Euler-Bernoulli element stiffness: axial = E*A/L, torsion = G*J/L, and bending terms 12EI/L^3, 6EI/L^2, 4EI/L, 2EI/L for both local y and z.
transform_global_stiffness applies T^T * K_local * T using the orientation's transformation matrix.
assemble_global_stiffness builds the dense global stiffness by validating node indices and scattering each element's global stiffness through its element DOF map.
reduce_system constrains the given restrained DOFs to zero displacement and returns the reduced system.
reduce_system_with_prescribed_displacements reduces the system for prescribed (possibly nonzero) boundary displacements.

reduce_system_for_boundary validates a square stiffness matrix and matching finite force vector, rejects out-of-range or repeated boundary DOFs, and adjusts free-DOF forces by subtracting stiffness contributions of prescribed displacements.

The sparse ordering is reverse Cuthill-McKee, chosen as the classic bandwidth/profile-reducing ordering for banded/branched frame topologies and as a pure breadth-first traversal admitting a fully deterministic formulation.
RCM determinism: the result is a pure function of the undirected graph; adjacency lists are symmetrized, sorted, and deduplicated so caller list order cannot change the result.
RCM determinism: connected components are processed in order of their lowest original node index.
RCM determinism: each component starts from a pseudo-peripheral node found by level-structure iteration, with every tie broken by ascending (degree, original index).

RCM determinism: breadth-first neighbor visits are ordered by ascending (degree, original index), and the concatenated order is reversed once at the end; no randomization, threading, or platform-dependent iteration order is used.

The factorization and solve are single-threaded straight-line f64 arithmetic with a fixed operation order, no reassociation/blocking/SIMD/parallel reduction, preserving byte-reproducibility like the dense path; repeat-run bitwise identity is asserted in tests.

A pivot at or below the guard fails as SingularPivot reporting both the profile-ordered index and the original pre-ordering index so the failure traces to a reduced DOF.
Accepted negative pivots are never silently absorbed: the report carries nonpositive_pivot_count and first location; nonpositive pivots indicate the reduced system is not positive definite.
pivot_condition_ratio_estimate is max|d|/min|d| over accepted LDL^T pivots, a documented conditioning proxy not a true condition number; no thresholds are encoded (governed by D-04).

Symmetric-input contract: the solver reads only one triangle; for any index pair it reads the original lower-triangle entry dense[max][min]. Input symmetry is the caller's contract, keeping construction deterministic under last-ulp asymmetry.

OpenPipeStress Unit Core Contract: DEL-02-02 defines the contract for unit-aware quantities and dimensional analysis in the domain core.
The unit core contract is structural: it does not ship protected standards data, proprietary dimensional tables, code-specific values, material allowables, SIF/flexibility factors, or vendor data.

DEC-018 accepted the D-01 unit-catalog basis on 2026-06-10: SI-canonical internal units, a closed SI/US display catalog, reviewed public definitional conversion constants, dual absolute/interval temperature semantics, explicit gauge/absolute pressure kinds with no silent atmospheric default, and a two-tier conversion-witness tolerance policy.

This crate is the Phase B1 crate-side implementation of DEC-018, providing the canonical dimension vocabulary, exponent-vector algebra, a deterministic unit catalog, and public definitional conversion constants recorded in code rather than protected standards data.

B1 provides affine absolute-temperature conversion separate from interval-temperature conversion, explicit gauge/absolute pressure conversion requiring caller-supplied reference and provenance on kind change, and finite-value and incompatible-dimension rejection.
B1 does not wire units into schemas, application fields, solver boundaries, reports, imports, exports, or rule-pack evaluation; those remain Phase B2/B3 handoffs.

Storage Convention: every physical quantity crossing a schema, solver, import/export, report, or rule-evaluation boundary must carry a magnitude, explicit unit reference, explicit dimension identifier, quantity kind, provenance for reliance-affecting values, and a missing-unit behavior.
Persisted project data should preserve the entered unit representation for audit and round-trip; hashed JSON payloads must use the project canonical JSON/JCS-compatible basis where applicable.

Dimensionless values are not a fallback for missing units; a value may be unitless only when its field is explicitly classified as dimensionless, ratio, percentage, or coefficient, otherwise missing unit metadata is a diagnostic.

Dimension Checking: the unit core owns dimensional compatibility checks for calculations, schemas, imports, exports, and rule evaluations; adapters and plugins must call through this contract instead of bypassing it.

Required operation behavior: addition, subtraction, comparison, and conversion require compatible dimensions; multiplication, division, and power must produce explicit derived dimensions; unknown dimensions remain TBD or produce blocking diagnostics.
Offset/reference-sensitive quantities, including temperature scale versus interval and gauge versus absolute pressure, require explicit semantics before conversion.

The PKG-02 canonical dimension vocabulary is: dimensionless, length, mass, time, temperature, temperature_interval, angle, rotation, force, moment, pressure, stress, area, volume, density, linear_stiffness, rotational_stiffness, displacement, velocity, acceleration, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, thermal_expansion_coefficient, second_moment_area, section_modulus, mass_per_length, volume_per_length, slope, and TBD.
The dimension vocabulary is a contract surface for checking structure; it is not a source of engineering design values.

Retired dimension aliases are not accepted: use temperature_interval for former temperature_difference, second_moment_area for former area_moment, and classify generic stiffness as linear_stiffness or rotational_stiffness.
Operation Rules: the unit contract records dimensional operation rules explicitly; implementations must not hide compatibility behavior in adapters, GUI, report rendering, or rule-pack evaluation.

Required operation categories: same-dimension (add, subtract, compare, convert); derived-dimension (multiply, divide, power); boundary validation (schema, import, export, rule evaluation); and explicit classification for dimensionless, ratio, percentage, and coefficient values.
Unsupported operation semantics are represented as blocking diagnostics or TBD decisions; B3 still owns the broader mixed-unit round-trip, conversion-witness, rejection, and D-04 tolerance corpus.
Conversion Provenance: each conversion declaration must identify source unit, target unit, dimension, transform kind, factor or offset representation, provenance, and redistribution/review status.

If a conversion source appears to come from protected standards content, proprietary vendor data, or undocumented commercial data, ingestion stops and the record is quarantined for human/legal review.

The crate exposes schema-facing metadata on each UnitDefinition as factor_representation, optional offset_representation, explicit ConversionProvenance, and ReviewStatus, forming the B2 binding point for showing conversion provenance.

ConversionProvenance::ConventionalPublicConstant is used where the transform depends on a reviewed conventional public constant (e.g., lbf/psi-family conversions through standard gravity); ProjectGovernedDecision is used for project-governed canonical bindings such as stiffness display units.
Missing-Unit Handling: missing solve-required or rule-check-required units are findings, never silent defaults.

Expected missing-unit handling: solve-required quantity missing unit is a blocking unit diagnostic; rule-pack input missing/incompatible unit is rule-check-blocking; weak/missing provenance yields warning or quarantine; unsupported special semantics block until accepted.

Schema diagnostic codes include missing unit, unknown unit, ambiguous unit, dimension mismatch, unsupported conversion, missing conversion provenance, unresolved offset/reference semantics, required dimensionless classification, and suspected protected unit data.

Accepted for B1 by DEC-018: the unit catalog and conversion source set, base dimension vector and derived-dimension rules, offset temperature and gauge/absolute pressure behavior, and SI-canonical calculation basis with display-unit transforms.

Remaining contract-visible handoffs include B2 schema/app/solver/report integration with entered-unit preservation, B3 conversion-witness and tolerance corpus under DEC-026, and angle/rotation behavior beyond cataloged rad/deg.

Code-specific values, protected standards content, proprietary vendor data, material allowables, SIF/flexibility factors, release/professional/certification/sealing/authentication claims, and code-compliance claims must not be filled by implementation convenience.
Each accepted decision affecting public schemas, persistent files, or external contracts should be recorded through the project ADR or equivalent decision-record discipline.
Downstream Obligations: solver, load, stress, rule-pack, report, GUI, API, and adapter implementations must preserve the unit boundary.

Unit checks support mechanics and rule evaluation but do not certify, seal, approve, authenticate, or declare code compliance; imports/exports must reject or flag missing, ambiguous, or incompatible units; rule evaluators must be unit-aware and deterministic.

Reports must disclose unit-system identity, diagnostics, assumptions, and provenance where relevant; tests must cover schema parsing, required dimensions and quantity fields, operation rules, incompatible dimensions, dimensionless classification, missing-unit diagnostics, alias ambiguity rejection, deterministic conversion, and absence of silent defaults.

Remaining TBDs and handoffs are not waived by the B1 crate; downstream work must continue surfacing missing/unsupported units, incompatible dimensions, unresolved schema bindings, missing provenance, and professional or code-compliance claims as findings rather than defaults.

UnitId enumerates the closed catalog of SI-canonical and US display units, including separate absolute and interval temperature units and dual stiffness bindings.
UnitId::catalog_id maps each unit to a stable catalog identifier string of the form unit:<name>.
UnitId::definition returns the UnitDefinition for each unit, pairing a symbol, dimension, and Transform (linear or affine) built from the public conversion constants.
DegreeCelsius uses an affine transform with offset 273.15 K, and DegreeFahrenheit an affine transform with factor 5/9 and offset 459.67*5/9, for absolute-temperature conversion.
UnitDefinition carries id, symbol, dimension, transform_to_canonical, canonical flag, factor_representation, optional offset_representation, ConversionProvenance, and ReviewStatus.
Transform holds factor, offset, and TransformKind; linear() builds a multiplicative transform, affine() an affine one; to_canonical computes value*factor+offset and canonical_to_unit its inverse.
TransformKind enumerates Identity, Multiplicative, and Affine, with schema strings identity/multiplicative/affine.
ConversionProvenance enumerates SiCanonical, ExactPublicDefinition, ConventionalPublicConstant, and ProjectGovernedDecision, with corresponding schema strings.
ReviewStatus enumerates Accepted, Pending, Rejected, Quarantined, and Tbd, with corresponding schema strings.
QuantityKind enumerates Absolute, Interval, Relative, Ratio, Percentage, Coefficient, Dimensionless, UnitBearing, and Tbd.
PressureKind enumerates Absolute and Gauge.
PressureReference holds value, unit, and provenance; new() requires a finite value, a Pressure-dimension unit, and non-empty provenance (else MissingPressureReferenceProvenance).
PressureReference::standard_atmosphere builds a reference at STANDARD_ATMOSPHERE_IN_PASCALS in Pascals from supplied provenance.
catalog() returns the static slice of cataloged UnitIds and catalog_definitions() yields their UnitDefinitions.
canonical_unit maps each dimension to its SI-canonical unit (Length->Meter, Pressure/Stress->Pascal, Temperature->Kelvin, etc.); Tbd has no canonical unit.
unit_by_symbol resolves a UnitId from a symbol and dimension, falling back to dimension-supporting matches, else UnknownUnit.
convert validates the value finite, rejects dimension mismatch and unresolved (Tbd) dimensions, then converts through the canonical basis.
convert_for_dimension converts between units bound to a requested semantic dimension, accepting units that support that dimension (e.g., Stress via Pressure units).
convert_quantity gates conversion by QuantityKind: temperature requires Absolute, temperature_interval requires Interval, pressure requires Absolute/Relative, else InvalidQuantityKind.
temperature_difference converts two absolute temperatures to Kelvin, subtracts, and reports the difference in a target interval unit.
shift_temperature adds an interval (converted to Kelvin interval) to an absolute temperature (converted to Kelvin) and returns the result in a target absolute unit.

convert_pressure_kind converts between gauge and absolute pressure, requiring an explicit PressureReference (MissingPressureReference if absent) and adding/subtracting the reference in Pascals on kind change.

UnitError enumerates UnknownDimension, RetiredDimensionAlias, UnknownUnit, DimensionMismatch, InvalidQuantityKind, MissingPressureReference, MissingPressureReferenceProvenance, NonFiniteInput, and UnresolvedDimension.
UnitError implements Display, including the message that gauge/absolute pressure conversion requires an explicit reference and that pressure reference requires non-empty provenance.
CATALOG is the static closed list of all cataloged UnitId entries.
def() assembles a UnitDefinition, marking canonical when the unit is the dimension's canonical unit and attaching factor/offset representation, provenance, and Accepted review status.

conversion_provenance classifies pound-force/psi/ksi family units as ConventionalPublicConstant, project stiffness/volume-per-length bindings as ProjectGovernedDecision, canonical units as SiCanonical, and the rest as ExactPublicDefinition.
offset_representation documents the affine offsets: 273.15 K at 0 degC and (459.67*5/9) K at 0 degF, each exact by definition.

factor_representation records a human-readable, auditable conversion-factor string per unit (e.g., 25.4 mm/in exact by definition; pound-force via 0.45359237 kg/lb * 9.80665 m/s^2 conventional standard gravity).
require_dimension errors with DimensionMismatch unless the unit's dimension equals the expected dimension.
validate_finite errors with NonFiniteInput unless the value is finite.

unit_supports_dimension allows a unit dimension to serve a requested dimension for accepted equivalences: Length/Displacement, Pressure/Stress, Angle/Rotation, Dimensionless/Slope, Area/VolumePerLength, and ForcePerLength/LinearStiffness.

units lib.rs contains a #[cfg(test)] tests module cross-checking the schema DimensionId enum against the crate vocabulary and verifying catalog metadata, conversions, temperature/pressure semantics, quantity-kind gating, and non-finite rejection.
